adapter.name: stanag4609
adapter.why_the_two_names_differ: The adapter takes the STANAG's number because STANAG 4609 is, in MISP-2019.1 SS C.1.2's own words, 'a covering document rather than a standalone document, which points directly to a version of the U.S. Motion Imagery Standards Profile (MISP)' - so there is no NATO document whose CONTENT could name the adapter, while the STANAG number is what an ICD, a NISP row and a national ratification record all call the feed. The fixture directory takes the content's name because a directory holds PAYLOADS and a payload is not a standard, which is the same split that puts adapter stanag4676's fixtures in fixtures/nits. The adapter-shaped content is the KLV metadata stream, so the directory is klv and the payload extension will be .klv.

rejected_directory_names.misp: Names the governing profile, which is a DOCUMENT - the pinned PDF would sit at fixtures/misp/spec/misb-misp-2019-1.pdf, a directory named after a file inside it. It also names the wrong layer: the MISP governs the imagery, the audio, the containers and the transport as well, and this adapter reads one of the five.
rejected_directory_names.misb: Names the publisher. fixtures/eurocontrol would have been wrong for CAT048 for the same reason.
rejected_directory_names.fmv: Rejected by the pinned text itself, MISP SS 2.1.1: 'FMV has no formal definition and conveys different meanings to different communities; therefore, the term FMV should not be used in any contractual language.' A fixture directory name is closer to contractual language than to prose.
rejected_directory_names.stanag4609: Would reproduce the bug commit 80b38d1 had to fix - three NITS PDFs sitting in a directory named for the adapter because a copy command took the adapter's name where the fixture directory's name was wanted.

the_normative_act.aim: The aim of this NATO standardization agreement (STANAG) is to respond to the following interoperability requirements.
the_normative_act.interoperability_requirement: To provide common methods for the generation, dissemination, exploitation and archive of Motion Imagery (MI) among National and NATO Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) systems.
the_normative_act.agreement: Participating nations agree to implement the following standard.
the_normative_act.standard: U.S. Motion Imagery Standards Board (MISB) Motion Imagery Standards Profile-2019.1 (MISP-2019.1)
the_normative_act.other_related_documents: U.S. Motion Imagery Standards Board (MISB) Motion Imagery Standards Profile-2019.1 (MISP-2019.1): Motion Imagery Handbook
the_normative_act.implementation_of_the_agreement: MISP-2019.1 defines the technical requirements for motion imagery formats, compression, metadata and transmission protocols for ISR systems and systems that manage and/or exploit motion imagery data.
the_normative_act.what_it_contains_that_is_technical: Nothing. The wrapper states no field, no encoding, no layout and no requirement of its own. Every technical requirement this adapter could implement is in the profile it promulgates, which is why there are two pins and not one.

delegated_specifications_held.what_this_is: The delegated documents this repository holds on disk. MISP-2019.1 delegates every field dictionary it relies on to a document published by somebody else, AND NOT EVERY DOCUMENT IT DELEGATES TO IS ONE, which is why this sentence says documents. Fourteen delegations are in scope: THIRTEEN are named in delegation_table below, and the fourteenth is the MISP-2019.1 Motion Imagery Handbook, park 10, which the WRAPPER names under OTHER RELATED DOCUMENTS and delegation_table does not carry. EIGHT of the fourteen are here - ST 0601.14, ST 0102.12, ST 0107.3, ST 1402.2, ST 1201.3, ST 1303.1, ST 1204.1 and ST 1301.2 - and this node holds TEN documents, because ST 0601.19 and EG 0601.1 are held and are not delegations. A document this repository holds and a delegation the profile makes are different things, and the tally counts the second. ST 0102.12 and ST 0601.14 are the exact editions the profile pins. ST 0601.19 is NOT - it is five major revisions later than the 0601.14 ref [53] cites - and it is retained as CONTEXT ONLY under reconciliation_ruling.ruling_st_0601: useful for the item-42 divergence note and for knowing where the standard went, and never a source of tag semantics for this row set. CORRECTED 2026-08-28 BY THE RULED ROUND, AND EVERY PART OF THE CORRECTION WAS ALREADY RULED ELSEWHERE IN THIS RECORD - nothing here is a new judgment about what a field dictionary is. (1) THE TERM. The opening read field dictionaries. FORMAT_COVERAGE.md says the same in its own words at its tally row. The repair was made at two sites on the day it was ruled and was not made at this one. (2) THE COUNT. It read THREE and never moved. provenance_ruling.page_as_source: The source of record for a MISB standard is its NSG Registry document page - https://nsgreg.nga.mil/doc/view?i=<n> - and not the URL the bytes arrived over. The page is stable, dereferenceable and states the registry's own view of the document's identity: its version, its registration status and what it supersedes.
provenance_ruling.hash_as_copy: The SHA-256 identifies the COPY THAT WAS READ, which is a different claim from the edition number. This is house style in every pin record here and this round is the first to prove why it is not pedantry: ST 0601.19's cover says 02 March 2023 and the copy on disk carries two amendment rows dated after that, under the same edition number and with no minor-version letter on the cover. The edition number cannot distinguish those two documents. The hash can.
provenance_ruling.why_download_urls_are_not_recorded: The registry serves documents over EPHEMERAL PRESIGNED LINKS. Such a URL expires, so recording one would put a dead string in the source field of a record whose whole purpose is to be checkable years later. The doc/view page is what a reader is sent to; the presigned link is a transport detail of one retrieval.
provenance_ruling.what_the_edition_date_field_means: The date the DOCUMENT states for itself, read off its own cover or front matter, and authoritative for this field where the document states one. Where the registry page states a date too, both are recorded and required to agree - see st_0102_12 below, where three independent statements of 22 June 2017 agree.
provenance_ruling.the_registry_pages_were_not_machine_veri: HONEST LIMIT ON THE SOURCE FIELD. Both doc/view URLs are recorded as the citable source and neither was retrieved by this round: nsgreg.nga.mil answers an automated GET with a CAPTCHA interstitial, so the page's stated version, registration status and supersession line could not be read mechanically. They are recorded as reported. Every fact this round ASSERTS about either document - hash, byte count, page count, edition date, title-page identity - was taken from the bytes on disk instead, which is the stronger source for those five and the reason the ruling below does not rest on the registry at all. The parks' reopen route is unaffected: a CAPTCHA is a bot gate, not an account gate, and a person with a browser is not blocked.

st_0601_14.document: MISB ST 0601.14, UAS Datalink Local Set
st_0601_14.edition_as_the_profile_cites_it: 'MISB ST 0601.14 UAS Datalink Local Set, Nov 2018' - MISP-2019.1 Appendix B reference [53], verbatim, and the 2019.1 Change Log agrees. The citation carries NO minor-version letter, which is the whole subject of the_copy_is_the_a_minor_revision below.
st_0601_14.registry_page_as_reported: Read from the document's page by the operator and recorded as reported, on the same footing as the two registry pages already in this record - see provenance_ruling.the_registry_pages_were_not_machine_verified_and_why, which still holds: nsgreg.nga.mil answers an automated GET with a CAPTCHA interstitial. Document ID 4739. Edition 'Version 1.14'. Edition date 01 November 2018. Status SUPERSEDED, 6 Jun 2019. Superseded by document 4803 (ST 0601.15). Supersedes document 4679 (ST 0601.13). Every fact this round ASSERTS about the copy - hash, byte count, page count, cover identity, cover date, revision history, tag table - was taken from the bytes on disk instead.
st_0601_14.superseded_is_not_withdrawn: EXPECTED AND ACCEPTABLE, and recorded so that nobody re-opens it as a defect. The profile froze its references in November 2018 and the registry moved on: ST 0601.14 was superseded on 6 June 2019 by 0601.15 and has been superseded four more times since. A profile that pins a revision pins the document that revision names, and that document does not stop being the pinned one when a later revision is registered - it stops being the CURRENT one. This is why parks.shared_exit_condition says 'obtain the EXACT version the delegation table pins (not the current one)'. Superseded entries stay registered and stay downloadable, which is what made this round possible; a WITHDRAWN entry would be a different fact and this one is not withdrawn.
st_0601_14.the_copy_is_the_a_minor_revision: THE KLV 9 HAZARD ARRIVING AT FETCH TIME RATHER THAN BEING FOUND LATER, and the reason this field exists before any tag was read. The registry serves this edition as ST0601.14a.pdf - a single-letter Minor Version that the citation 'MISB ST 0601.14' does not carry and cannot carry. THE FILENAME IS KEPT AS THE REGISTRY SERVES IT, deliberately and not as an oversight: the FILENAME states the copy, the `edition` field states the edition the profile cites ('0601.14'), and the SHA-256 states the identity. Renaming the file to ST0601.14.pdf would make the directory listing agree with the citation by destroying the one piece of evidence that they differ. Cross-reference ambiguity_register KLV 9, which is the same coming-apart discovered in ST 0601.19 by a check nobody asked for, and KLV 10, which is this one.
st_0601_14.what_the_document_itself_says_about_the_: READ FROM THE PDF's OWN COVER AND REVISION HISTORY rather than inferred from the filename. (1) The cover prints 'MISB ST 0601.14a' - the letter is on the document, not only on the file. (2) Section 2 states the convention: 'In the event of a MISB document correction, the corrected document will have a single letter Minor Version appended to the Major Version number per the MISB Document Development Process [1]. For example, corrections to ST 0001.2, which has a Major Version of 2, result in a new version titled ST 0001.2a, which includes a Minor Version of "a". The MISB will not update the referring document (this document) with the Minor Version number change. When acquiring any MISB reference listed below from an NGA repository the latest version may be either a Major or Minor Version.' So the profile's failure to cite the 'a' is not an error in the profile - it is the convention working as written. (3) The revision history table on PDF page 3 says what the 'a' CHANGED, in one line: 'ST 0601.14a | 05/1/2020 | Corrected table headers in Item 47 - Generic Flags.' One corrected table header, in one item, in a 218-page document.
st_0601_14.edition_date_read_from: The document's own cover, which prints 'MISB ST 0601.14a' and '1 May 2020', and the footer of all 218 pages, which repeats '1 May 2020'. Per provenance_ruling.what_the_edition_date_field_means - the date the DOCUMENT states for itself, authoritative for this field where the document states one - this field is 1 May 2020. IT IS THE DATE OF THE 'a' MINOR REVISION AND NOT OF EDITION .14, and the next field is why that is a distinction and not a contradiction.
st_0601_14.the_two_dates_are_two_different_facts_an: NOT A CONTRADICTION, and it was checked as one before it was recorded as a distinction. The registry reports edition date 01 November 2018 for Version 1.14; the cover of this copy says 1 May 2020. Those date different things, and THE DOCUMENT ITSELF SAYS SO: its revision history table opens with the row 'ST 0601.14 | 11/1/2018' - 1 November 2018, in the MM/D/YYYY form this publisher uses throughout - and then adds 'ST 0601.14a | 05/1/2020'. eg_0601_1.the_document_is_an_EG_AND_NOT_AN_ST_AND_: THERE IS NO 'MISB ST 0601.1'. Edition 1 of the 0601 series was published as an ENGINEERING GUIDELINE - MISB EG 0601.1 - and the series became a Standard at 0601.2. Park 13 was opened under the name 'MISB ST 0601.1', which is a document that was never published, and the name was not this repository's invention: ST 0601.14a SS 8.65 defines item 65's value range as '1..255 corresponds to document revisions MISB ST 0601.1 thru MISB ST 0601.255', projecting the current series name back onto twelve editions that carried a different one. Edition 1's own SS 7.65 states the same range as 'EG0601.1 thru EG0601.255'. So a reader following SS 8.65 to the letter is sent to a document that does not exist, and this pin is the document SS 8.65's '0601.1' DENOTES. Registered as KLV 15.

Both official routes were tried and both refused an automated GET: gwg.nga.mil - the MISB's own document host - answers HTTP 403 from CloudFront at every ST0601.N.pdf and EG0601.N.pdf pattern tried, with and without a browser User-Agent and Referer; and nsgreg.nga.mil answers with an F5 JavaScript interstitial ('Please enable JavaScript to view the page content'), which is the same wall provenance_ruling.the_registry_pages_were_not_machine_verified_and_why already records, now met on the document route rather than the page route. So the bytes came from the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine. REGISTRY ABSENCE IS RECORDED AS A PROVENANCE CAVEAT AND NOT AS A DEFECT IN THE COPY: what the mirror costs is the third leg of the disjunction - st_0107_3 could check its edition date against a registry page's agreement and this cannot - and what it does not cost is the hash, which identifies the COPY THAT WAS READ and never claimed more. What the snapshot carries that a bare mirror could not: the URL it archives is gwg.nga.mil's OWN, so the record states which origin served these bytes and on what date they were served.

rfc_2781.document: IETF RFC 2781, UTF-16, an encoding of ISO 10646
rfc_2781.edition: RFC 2781, February 2000 — RFCs are not revised; a successor would be a different number
rfc_2781.THE_EDITION_FIELD_IS_A_DIFFERENT_KIND_OF: EVERY OTHER NODE'S `edition` NAMES ONE REVISION OF A DOCUMENT THAT HAS OTHERS. ST 0601.14 has a .19; ST 336:2017 has a :2007 and both are held; ST 0102.12 carries requirements numbered ST 0102.10-xx because its own predecessor wrote them. That is the shape this field is for, and it is why `reconciliation_ruling` and `edition_history` exist at all. **THE IETF DOES NOT WORK THAT WAY.** An RFC is immutable once published: a change is a NEW NUMBER that obsoletes or updates the old one, and the old text stays served and correct as a historical record. So there is no edition to get wrong here, and the field says so rather than printing a version string that would invite a reader to go looking for a later one. VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSERTED FROM GENERAL KNOWLEDGE: the RFC Editor's info page for 2781 carries no `Obsoleted by` row, no `Updated by` row, and no `Obsoletes`/`Updates` row — the four strings do not occur in the 177 626 bytes of the page — and the errata search returns 'No matching errata found'. So the text below is the whole of what the IETF has ever published under this number.
rfc_2781.why_both_a_source_and_a_route_are_record: ON THE ST 336 PRECEDENT AND FOR ITS REASON, which is stated at `st_336_2007.why_both_a_source_and_a_route_are_recorded_here`. The MISB nodes record no download URL because the NSG Registry serves presigned, expiring links and a URL that expires is not a provenance record. That reasoning does not reach this pin: `www.rfc-editor.org` is the publisher's own host and `/rfc/rfc2781.txt` is a stable path under it — no query string, no signature, no expiry parameter — so it is a durable locator of the same kind the info page is, and recording it costs nothing and buys a reader the exact bytes. THE ROUTE WAS READ OFF THE PUBLISHER'S PAGE AND NOT GUESSED: the info page's Formats block names two formats and its anchor hrefs are `/rfc/rfc2781.txt` and `/rfc/rfc2781.html`. The surface round additionally probed the two plausible PDF shapes — `/rfc/pdfrfc/rfc2781.txt.pdf` and `/rfc/rfc2781.pdf` — and both answered 404, so the absence of a PDF is a fact about the DOCUMENT and not about one guessed path.
rfc_2781.why_this_node_carries_a_format_field_and: RULED AT `text_pin_ruling.the_fields_a_text_pin_carries`: a node WITHOUT the field is a PDF. rfc_2781.pages_method: THE PAGINATED-TEXT VARIANT, ruled 2026-09-04 and recorded at `page_count_method.the_paginated_text_variant_ruled_2026_09_04`. THREE TERMS, ALL THREE REPORTED: form feeds (0x0C) counted — **14**; `[Page N]` footers counted — **14**; the highest footer number — **14**. All three agree, so the count is 14. Two corroborations beyond the agreement: the footer numbers form the consecutive run 1 through 14 with no gap, and splitting the text on 0x0C yields fifteen segments whose last is exactly one newline — so there is no unfootered trailing page that the footer count could have dropped.
rfc_2781.lines_method: **THE COUNT OF `\n` BYTES, WHICH IS `wc -l` SEMANTICS: 787.** Ruled, because the obvious alternative disagrees. Python's `str.splitlines()` reports **801**, because it treats the form feed 0x0C as a line terminator and this document carries 14 of them: 801 - 787 = 14, exactly the page count. A `lines` value taken one way and checked the other therefore differs by the page count WITH NO ERROR ANYWHERE, which is the same silent-disagreement shape `gates/pdf_text.py` exists for. Both figures are recorded — here and at `text_pin_ruling.the_lines_definition_and_the_787_versus_801_trap` — so a reader who computes the other one finds the disagreement explained where they meet it instead of concluding the pin is wrong.

The adjudication round introduced the PDF document-information dictionary as the 'cheapest useful read in the set' and calibrated it on the four held 0601 documents, where /CreationDate equalled the cover date exactly for three and post-dated it by four days for the initial release. ST 1402.2 then post-dated by 47 days. THE FOUR DOCUMENTS PINNED ON 2026-08-27 EVENING POST-DATE THEIR COVERS BY 462, 63, 47 AND 288 DAYS. So across the nine samples now held the delta runs 0 to 462 days and the field corroborates only that a file was PRODUCED NO EARLIER THAN its cover date. AT 462 DAYS IT DOES NOT CORROBORATE EVEN THE YEAR, which is exactly the claim st_1402_2's node makes for it ('corroborates the YEAR and nothing finer') - so that sentence is true of that document and is NOT true as a general rule, and it is narrowed here rather than edited there, on entry 5's rule that a closed record which quietly updates its own history is a record nobody can date. WHAT THE FIELD IS STILL GOOD FOR: a LOWER bound, and detecting a file re-saved long after its cover - which is itself the KLV 9 / KLV 10 hazard seen from the file side rather than the page side. What it is NOT good for is corroborating a cover date, which is what it was first used to do. AMENDED 2026-08-28 BY THE REPAIR ROUND, AND THE AMENDMENT IS ABOUT COVERAGE RATHER THAN CORRECTNESS. Everything above re-derived from the held bytes today and all nine sampled lags match this record exactly - 0 for EG 0601.1, 4 for the 0601 initial release, 0 for ST 0601.4, 0 for ST 0601.8, 47 for ST 1402.2, 462 for ST 1201.3, 63 for ST 1303.1, 47 for ST 1204.1 and 288 for ST 1301.2. WHAT WAS MISSING IS THE SENTENCE SAYING WHAT THE SAMPLE COVERS. It is NINE OF THIRTEEN, and the thirteen are the held MISB documents that carry a DAY-PRECISION cover date - fifteen PDFs sit in this directory and two of them are not in that set: the NATO STANAG 4609 Edition 5 wrapper is not a MISB document, and MISP-2019.1's cover states 'November 2018', a month with no day, so no lag in days exists to measure for it. THE FOUR UNSAMPLED SPLIT TWO AND TWO. Two are EXCLUDED FOR CAUSE and their lags are not evidence about production delay: ST 0601.19 at 853 days and ST 0601.14a at 595 are the KLV 9 and KLV 10 copies, whose covers are known not to describe their contents, so what their lag measures is an undeclared amendment. The other two are CLEAN AND WERE SIMPLY NEVER SAMPLED - ST 0107.3 at 63 days, and ST 0102.12 at 567. ST 0102.12 IS THE SHARPEST CASE IN THE WHOLE SET AND IT WAS THE ONE LEFT OUT: its cover date is the one this record says three independent statements agree on and it carries a single revision-history row, so it is the least ambiguous document here and it post-dates its own cover by more than any sampled document does. THE WIDEST LAG OVER CLEANLY-DATED COPIES IS THEREFORE 567 DAYS AND NOT 462, and if the NATO wrapper is admitted it is 617. The conclusion above is UNCHANGED IN DIRECTION AND STRENGTHENED IN DEGREE: the field establishes that a file was produced no earlier than its cover and nothing else, it is a lower bound and a detector of late re-saves, and it is not evidence for a cover date. ruling_st_0601.ruling: MISMATCH, and option (b): THE CITED EDITION IS REQUIRED. RESOLVED 2026-08-26 - the cited edition was fetched. See resolution_2026_08_26 below, which is the operative ruling now; the fields above it are the stop that produced the fetch and are kept because a ruling whose grounds are deleted once it is discharged cannot be audited.
grounds: THE REPOSITORY HAS ALREADY RULED THIS, and consistency is not optional. This record's parks.shared_exit_condition, written in an earlier round and covering parks 1-7 and 9-12, reads: 'obtain the EXACT version the delegation table pins (not "the current one" - the profile pins a revision and a later revision is a different document)'. ST 0601 is park 1. Reading 0601.19 against the profile would overturn a standing ruling in passing, which is the failure mode this record's correction_2026_08_25 field exists to record an instance of.

FORMAT_COVERAGE.md's park 1 row already states the hazard in its own words: 'Version .14 specifically: ST 0601 has revisions on both sides of it, and a tag added in a later revision decoded against an earlier one is a plausible number in the wrong field.' That is not a new argument produced to justify a stop; it is the argument the park was opened with.

OPTION (a) IS NOT COMPLETABLE FROM THE COPY IN HAND, which is the decisive practical ground. Option (a) requires recording 'whether any [tags] were added or changed meaning after the cited edition'. ST 0601.19's Table 1 has columns Tag, Name, Units, Format, Len, SDCC, MUL and Description - there is NO column stating which revision introduced an item - and its revision history table carries rows for .19 and its two later amendments and NO rows for .15, .16, .17 or .18. So for any given tag, 'did this exist in .14' cannot be answered from 0601.19 alone. Ruling (a) would mean asserting a delta this round cannot compute.

AND THE HAZARD IS DEMONSTRATED, not hypothetical. 0601.19's revision history records 'Resolved item 42 ambiguity (i.e., MSL or HAE)' on 06/11/2025 - a change to what a tag MEANS, on the mean-sea-level-versus-height-above-ellipsoid axis, which is exactly the class of change that yields a plausible number in the wrong field. It also records 'Added Item 143 - Metadata Substream ID (MSID)' for .19 itself. One documented semantic change and one documented addition, inside the only revision window the document describes.
ruling_st_0601.what_the_document_does_let_us_bound: Recorded because it is real and because it is what a later round would start from, NOT as a basis for proceeding. ST 0601 stamps each requirement with the version that introduced it, so the post-.14 REQUIREMENT delta is enumerable from 0601.19 alone: twelve requirements, being ST 0601.15-36, ST 0601.17-37 through ST 0601.17-40, and ST 0601.19-41 through ST 0601.19-47. No requirement names .16 or .18. Appendix A additionally lists retired requirements with the version each came from, including five at ST 0601.14. This bounds the REQUIREMENT delta; it does not bound the ITEM delta, and the item delta is the one a tag table would need.

resolution_2026_08_26.why_the_a_does_not_reopen_the_mismatch: Because a Minor Version is a correction to a Major Version and not a different edition, on the document's own statement of the rule quoted at delegated_specifications_held.st_0601_14.what_the_document_itself_says_about_the_a, and because the one thing the 'a' changed is recorded in one line of the revision history: 'Corrected table headers in Item 47 - Generic Flags.' resolution_2026_08_26.what_this_closes: Park 1. Both halves of parks.shared_exit_condition are discharged: the exact version the delegation table pins is obtained and pinned by SHA-256, byte count and page count with its title-page identity read, AND the row set that document supports is written - 141 rows, at tag_table_st_0601_14 here and in FORMAT_COVERAGE.md. See parks.what_this_round_changed.
resolution_2026_08_26.what_this_does_NOT_close: Everything the row set is still blocked on, and the list is not short. Parks 4 and 8 (ST 0107.3 and SMPTE ST 336:2017) still govern how an item is FOUND in the octets, so not one of the 141 rows can be read from a stream yet. Park 3 (ST 0603.5) still owns the epoch, so item 2 is an integer and not an instant. Park 5 (ST 1201.3) still owns the IMAPB ranges. The tag table says what each item MEANS and what its length and format are; it does not say where the item begins.
resolution_2026_08_26.the_prior_ruling_is_not_overturned: It is DISCHARGED, which is a different thing and the distinction matters here. The prior round ruled that .19 may not substitute for .14 and stopped. Nothing about that ruling was wrong and this round did not read around it - it did the thing the ruling named as the way out. correction_2026_08_25 records what happens when a standing ruling is overturned in passing; this is the other case, and the two should not look alike in the record.

ruling_stanag_4609_edition_5.question: What does the wrapper itself cite for ST 0601 and ST 0102, and does it agree with MISP-2019.1?
ruling_stanag_4609_edition_5.grounds: STANAG 4609 Edition 5 is five pages and its normative content is read in full. Its AGREEMENT clause reads 'Participating nations agree to implement the following standard' and its STANDARD clause names exactly one document: 'U.S. Motion Imagery Standards Board (MISB) Motion Imagery Standards Profile-2019.1 (MISP-2019.1)'. Its OTHER RELATED DOCUMENTS clause names one more, the MISP-2019.1 Motion Imagery Handbook. The strings '0601' and '0102' do not occur in the document at all. It has no reference list of its own.
ruling_stanag_4609_edition_5.ruling: NO CONFLICT TO RECONCILE, and this is a finding rather than an absence of one. The wrapper cites no edition of either document, so it cannot agree or disagree with MISP-2019.1 about one. It delegates the entire question, which makes MISP-2019.1 the SOLE authority for what edition of ST 0601 and ST 0102 governs a STANAG 4609 Edition 5 feed. The two rulings above are therefore the whole of the reconciliation; there is no third opinion to weigh.
ruling_stanag_4609_edition_5.consistent_with_what_this_record_already: wrapper.the_normative_act.what_it_contains_that_is_technical already reads 'Nothing. The wrapper states no field, no encoding, no layout and no requirement of its own.' This round asked a narrower question of the same five pages and got the same answer, which is a corroboration and not a new claim.
ruling_stanag_4609_edition_5.the_one_edition_disagreement_the_wrapper: Not about ST 0601 or ST 0102, and already recorded as ambiguity KLV 3: the wrapper is Edition 5 and MISP-2019.1's Appendix B reference [1] cites 'NATO STANAG 4609: NATO Digital Motion Imagery Standard, Edition 4, 19 Dec 2016' - the profile refers to the edition before the one that promulgates it. Re-read and confirmed verbatim this round.

tag_table_st_0601_14.what_this_is: MISB ST 0601.14's Table 1, 'UAS Datalink Local Set', transcribed in full. This is the field dictionary of the airborne UAS collection - the thing MISP-2019.1 SS 4.4.4.1 delegates and names without describing, and the reason park 1 was the largest park in this section. The Tag, Name, Units, Format, Len and CDM-field columns of FORMAT_COVERAGE.md's ST 0601 row set are generated from `items` below, so those cannot disagree; that row set's Notes column additionally carries this round's per-item findings, which are prose and live there.
tag_table_st_0601_14.source: ST 0601.14a, Table 1, PDF pages 13-17. The copy pinned at delegated_specifications_held.st_0601_14.
tag_table_st_0601_14.the_edition_this_is_read_from: ST 0601.14 and NOT ST 0601.19. ST 0601.14 - this copy, this hash - is the authoritative tag table for this row set; ST 0601.19 remains pinned as context only and is never a source of tag semantics here. Ruled at reconciliation_ruling.ruling_st_0601.resolution_2026_08_26.
tag_table_st_0601_14.how_it_was_transcribed: BY THE TABLE'S OWN DRAWN GRID, not by reading lines off a text dump, and the difference is not cosmetic. Table 1's Description cells wrap to two and three lines and are vertically CENTRED in their row, so a description line frequently sits above the line carrying its own Tag number and below the previous row's. A reader-order text extraction therefore attaches the tail of item 1's description to item 2 - which it did, on the first attempt, silently and plausibly. The transcription instead reads the page's vector rectangles: the column boundaries are the table's own vertical rules, at x = 75.4, 98.4, 217.3, 243.2, 274.2, 292.2, 317.4, 339.0 and 536.4 on every one of the five pages, and the row boundaries are the horizontal cell borders drawn in the Tag column. Each text item is then assigned to the cell its own (x, y) falls in. A cell is what the document draws, so that is what is read.
tag_table_st_0601_14.cross_check_that_makes_the_transcription: THE DOCUMENT STATES THE SAME MAPPING TWICE AND BOTH WERE READ. Table 2, 'Tags Sorted by Name' (PDF pages 17-18), is the same 141 items in alphabetical order across three name/tag column pairs - a completely different grid, extracted by the same method and independently. The two agree on all 141 tag-to-name pairs: no tag in one and not the other, and no name disagreement. Additionally the tag numbers run 1 through 141 with no gap and no duplicate, which is the positive control a summary table can offer about itself.
tag_table_st_0601_14.columns_as_the_document_defines_them: Tag, Name, Units, Format, Len, SDCC, MUL, Description - and the document defines four of them in prose immediately above the table. Units: 'None' means the value is not a measurement, 'Set' or 'Pack' means the value is a collection, 'All other Units are SI enumerations'. Format: 'the item's KLV format for the Value'. Length: 'the nominal length of the value. This may be a required length or variable length' - which is what 'V' means in the length column here. SDCC: whether the item may appear in a Standard Deviation Correlation Coefficient Floating Length Pack, whose own layout is MISB ST 1010.3's. MUL: whether the item may have multiple instances in one Local Set instance.
tag_table_st_0601_14.the_one_note_the_document_attaches_to_th: Quoted because it is a trap and the document says so itself: 'Several Local Set items have the same UL Key but differ in its Type. For example, Tag 22-Target Width, uses a Type of uint16, and Tag 96-Target Width Extended, uses a Type of IMAPB. The Key for both, which is the same, has a MISB ST 0807 dictionary data type of "float". This is an allowed practice, where this document specifies (or overrides) the metadata item's format within the dictionary.' So a decoder keyed on the 16-byte Universal Label alone cannot tell tag 22 from tag 96, and the LOCAL SET TAG is the discriminator. Recorded here rather than in a row, because it is a property of the table.

what_changed_between_14_and_19.what_this_is: MEASURED, from both documents, now that both are in hand - and recorded as a NOTE and never as a source. Not one value in the 141 rows above comes from .19. This node exists so that a reader can see exactly how large the hazard park 1 was opened on turned out to be, and so that the next round to move to a later edition knows what it is moving.
what_changed_between_14_and_19.items_added_in_19: Two: 142 View Domain, and 143 Metadata Substream ID Pack.
what_changed_between_14_and_19.items_removed_in_19: None. All 141 items of .14 survive into .19 at the same tag numbers.
what_changed_between_14_and_19.items_renamed: One: tag 72, 'Event Start Time - UTC' in .14, 'Event Start Time' in .19.
what_changed_between_14_and_19.structural_columns: IDENTICAL on all 141 shared items - Units, Format, Len, SDCC and MUL agree everywhere. This is the reassuring half and it should be read carefully: it means the wire FORM of every .14 item is unchanged in .19, so a .19 stream decoded against this table would not produce a wrong-length read on any shared item. It does not mean the meanings are unchanged.
what_changed_between_14_and_19.descriptions_changed_in_table_1: Eight of 141, and seven are editorial - a comma after 'e.g.', 'Galaleo' corrected to 'Galileo', 'takeoff' to 'take-off', 'Tag' to 'Item' in the cross-references at 137 and 139, and two shortened phrasings at 45 and 126. The eighth, item 136 Leap Seconds, is a real clarification: '.14: Number of leap seconds to adjust Precision Time Stamp (Tag 2) to UTC' against '.19: Number of leap seconds since MISP Epoch to use when converting Precision Time Stamp (Item 2) to UTC'.
what_changed_between_14_and_19.AND THE ONE THAT MATTERS IS NOT IN THAT: ITEM 42's SUMMARY ROW IS BYTE-FOR-BYTE IDENTICAL IN .14 AND .19. Both read 'Calculated target elevation'. The MSL-versus-HAE resolution that .19's revision history announces - 'Resolved item 42 ambiguity (i.e., MSL or HAE)', 06/11/2025 - lives ENTIRELY in the per-item detail section SS 8.42, where .19 adds 'conditionally either MSL or HAE' to the description line, a bullet reading 'Depending on items 25 and/or 78, the measurement base is either MSL or HAE', and three paragraphs of rules keyed on whether items 25 and 78 are present. THIS IS THE FINDING OF THE COMPARISON: a tag table transcribed from Table 1 alone is blind to the single documented semantic change in the whole window. Table 1 is a summary and the per-item sections are the specification, and this round can only say that because it read both.
what_changed_between_14_and_19.what_the_row_set_does_with_it: Records .14's semantics as normative and the divergence as a note, which is what item 42's row does. .14's SS 8.42 states a range, a mapping, a resolution and a recommendation, and states NO datum. So the .14 semantics ARE 'elevation, datum unstated', and that is what the row carries. Importing .19's resolution would be reading the row set against a document this ruling excludes, and it would be doing so at the one item where the two documents actually differ.

what_ST_0601_14_settles_that_the_profile.why_this_node_exists: A CORRECTION TO THE REACH OF TWO EARLIER FINDINGS, and it was found by reading item 2's own section rather than by being looked for. Settlement 3 and register entry KLV 6 are both about what MISP-2019.1 does NOT state, and both are still exactly true about MISP-2019.1. What this round can now add is that the delegated dictionary states it, and the whole discipline of this section is the difference between 'the pinned documents do not say' and 'nobody has read the document that says'.
what_ST_0601_14_settles_that_the_profile.the_epoch_IS_stated_here_and_it_is_state: SS 6.4, verbatim: 'Every UAS Datalink LS packet is required to include a Precision Time Stamp representing absolute time as defined in MISB ST 0603 [4]. The Precision Time Stamp (Tag 2) is an eight-byte unsigned integer counter of the number of SI Seconds (in microseconds) which have elapsed since midnight (00:00:00), January 1, 1970 (1970-01-01T00:00:00Z). Note: this time does not include leap seconds and therefore the Precision Time Stamp does not represent UTC.' SS 8.2 states it again in its own bullet and again in its Details paragraph. So epoch, unit, resolution and leap-second treatment are all read from a pinned document.
what_ST_0601_14_settles_that_the_profile.what_this_corrects_in_settlement_3: NOT THE FINDING - THE REACH. Settlement 3's evidence stands unaltered: `epoch`, `1970`, `microsecond` and `leap` occur zero times in MISP-2019.1's 73 pages, and the premise that the PROFILE fixes the epoch was and is false. What changes is the consequence drawn from it. The old consequence was that this repository could not state the epoch at all without writing down something it had not read. It has now read it, in the document the profile delegates to, and the value is stated with both loci. The rule was never 'do not write an epoch'; it was 'do not write one from memory', and that rule is what allows this.
what_ST_0601_14_settles_that_the_profile.what_this_corrects_in_KLV_6: KLV 6 says nothing in the profile requires a standalone metadata stream to carry an absolute time, resting on the circularity of a requirement that is 'mandatory for Metadata packets which include a Metadata item for a timestamp'. Still true of the profile. ST 0601.14 closes it from the other side for THIS local set and only for this one: SS 6.4 requires the Precision Time Stamp in every UAS Datalink LS packet, Table 1 and SS 8.2 mark item 2 Mandatory, and item 65 is Mandatory with it. A conformant UAS Datalink LS packet therefore always carries an absolute time. That is a fact about ST 0601.14's local set, not about KLV streams in general, and KLV 6 stays in the register because the general claim is the one it makes.
what_ST_0601_14_settles_that_the_profile.what_it_does_NOT_settle_and_why_park_3_s: Three things. FIRST, ST 0603.5 remains the normative definition - SS 6.4 says the Precision Time Stamp represents absolute time 'as defined in MISB ST 0603 [4]' and ST 0601.14 is restating it, so a conflict between the two is resolved by a document not held. SECOND, items 136 (Leap Seconds) and 137 (Correction Offset) exist precisely to convert this scale to UTC and their own semantics are ST 0603's - and .19 later rewrote item 136's summary line to name a 'MISP Epoch', a term ST 0601.14 does not use. THIRD, what to CALL a count of SI seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z that excludes leap seconds is exactly the TAI-versus-UTC question park 3's row says it decides, and ST 0601.14 answers only the negative half: not UTC. So the row for item 2 can now state its epoch, and park 3 stays open.
what_ST_0601_14_settles_that_the_profile.the_reference_agrees_with_the_profile_wh: ST 0601.14's own reference [4] reads 'MISB ST 0603.5 MISP Time System and Timestamps, Oct 2017' - the same revision MISP-2019.1's Appendix B pins for park 3, and the same date. Two independently-pinned documents naming the same revision of a third is the corroboration delegation_table.entries was built to make checkable, and this is the first time it has been available from both sides.

tag_table_st_0102_12.what_this_is: MISB ST 0102.12's §6.7 Table 2, 'Security Metadata Local Set Elements', transcribed in full — SEVENTEEN rows, each with the columns the document defines and with the §6.1.n element definition the row points at. This is the field dictionary of the security marking a UAS Datalink LS packet carries in ST 0601 item 48, and it is the artefact half of park 2's exit condition. Written in tag_table_st_0601_14's shape deliberately: the same node names, the same obligation to state how the transcription was made and what makes it checkable, and the same rule that the FORMAT_COVERAGE.md row set is generated from `items` below so the two cannot disagree. WHAT IS DIFFERENT AND IS NOT SMOOTHED OVER: park 1's table could be checked against the document's own 26 worked examples and this one cannot, because ST 0102.12 prints none.
tag_table_st_0102_12.source: ST 0102.12, §6.7 Table 2, PDF pages 13-14, plus §6.1.1-§6.1.17 on pages 5-9 for the element definitions. The copy pinned at delegated_specifications_held.st_0102_12 — SHA-256 20d40b5237cdcd2f486547add8eee238e37d5a6b11b7e0aca306be0785eca267, 514842 bytes, 18 pages, re-digested from disk at the start of this round and matching.
tag_table_st_0102_12.the_edition_this_is_read_from: ST 0102.12, and there is no second edition to rule against — unlike ST 0601, where .14 and .19 are both held and reconciliation_ruling.ruling_st_0601 had to name one. The profile pins 0102.12 (MISP-2019.1 Appendix B ref [55]), this copy is 0102.12, and its revision history carries a single row whose date is the cover's. ruling_st_0102 already closed that question.
tag_table_st_0102_12.the_carrier_and_why_it_is_the_LOCAL_set: ST 0601.14a §8.48 Tag 48 Security Local Set, Description 'MISB ST 0102 local let Security Metadata items' (the document's own typo for 'local set', preserved), Format 'KLV set', Length 'Variable', Max Length 'Not Limited', Required in LS? 'Optional'. Its two bullets: 'Use the MISB ST 0102 Local Set tags within the MISB ST 0601 item 48' and 'The length field is the size of all MISB ST 0102 metadata items to be packaged within item 48'. Its §8.48.1 Details: 'MISB ST 0102 [14] allows for the use of either Universal Set or Local Set methods. However, to minimize bandwidth when incorporating MISB ST 0102 into an instance of the UAS Datalink LS, the Local Set method is required.' And `ST 0601.14-31`: 'When incorporating the ST 0102 Security Metadata set into an instance of the UAS Datalink Local Set, the ST 0102 format shall use the Local Set format.' §8.48's Example KLV Item row prints Tag 30 (hex for 48), a Len of '-' and a Value of 'N/A' — SO THE DELEGATING DOCUMENT PRINTS NO WORKED EXAMPLE EITHER, and neither of the two documents behind this codec supplies one
tag_table_st_0102_12.the_universal_set_is_OUT_OF_SCOPE_and_th: §6.6 defines a Security Metadata UNIVERSAL Set carrying the same seventeen elements under 16-byte keys, registered at 06 0E 2B 34 02 01 01 01 02 08 02 00 00 00 00 00 (CRC 31942), and Table 1 lists its constituents. NOT TRANSCRIBED, on the delegating document's own sentence rather than on convenience: ST 0601.14a §8.48.1 reads 'MISB ST 0102 [14] allows for the use of either Universal Set or Local Set methods. However, to minimize bandwidth when incorporating MISB ST 0102 into an instance of the UAS Datalink LS, the Local Set method is required', and `ST 0601.14-31` makes it a shall. Item 48 carries the Local Set; the Universal Set is a different carrier and this round wrote no row for it. Table 1 WAS READ — it is one of the four cross-checks below — and reading a table to check another is not transcribing it.
tag_table_st_0102_12.how_it_was_transcribed: FROM THE DOCUMENT'S OWN TWO STATEMENTS OF THE SAME SEVENTEEN ELEMENTS, read separately and then compared, and NOT by trusting one extraction. Table 2's cells wrap heavily — tag 2's Allowed Values cell alone runs sixteen lines — so the columns were read per row against `gates/pdf_text.py`'s normalise-and-join rule and each row was then located by walking the tag sequence forward over the normalised text rather than by matching a line-anchored pattern, which is the trap ST 0601.14a's Table 1 sprang on the park 1 round at tag 105. The §6.1.n definitions were read from the prose, which does not wrap into columns, and each was matched to its row BY NAME rather than by position. WHAT THAT CATCHES: a row silently absorbing a neighbour's Allowed Values, which is the only way seventeen rows could read as seventeen and still be wrong.
tag_table_st_0102_12.cross_check_that_makes_the_transcription: THE DOCUMENT STATES THE SAME SEVENTEEN ELEMENTS TWICE AND BOTH WERE READ, WHICH IS PARK 1'S ARRANGEMENT REACHED BY A SECOND DOCUMENT. §6.7's Table 2 draws seventeen tag rows — 1 through 14, then 22, 23, 24 — and §6.1 carries seventeen numbered subsections, §6.1.1 through §6.1.17, one per element and in the same order. The two agree on all seventeen names with no element in one and not the other. A THIRD statement checks the three elements that matter most: §6.8 gives conversion rules between the Universal and Local Set forms and has EXACTLY THREE subsections — §6.8.1 Security Classification, §6.8.2 Classifying Country and Releasing Instructions Country Code, §6.8.3 Object Country Coding Method — which are exactly the three rows whose Table 2 Data Type reads `uint8` where Table 1's reads text. AND A FOURTH, over the same rows from the other side: §6.1's Table 1 for the Universal Set lists the same seventeen elements under 16-byte keys, so a row present in one carrier and absent from the other would show. WHAT THIS CANNOT DO, AND `klv_uas_codec` CAN: check a decoded value against the document's own worked example, because ST 0102.12 prints none
tag_table_st_0102_12.the_count_read_off_the_documents_own_tab: SEVENTEEN, and the arithmetic that makes it checkable rather than counted once. Table 2 draws rows for tags 1 through 14 — fourteen — and then 22, 23 and 24 — three. 14 + 3 = 17. The presence column splits the same seventeen a second way and independently: SIX Required (tags 1, 2, 3, 12, 13, 22), EIGHT Context (4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11) and THREE Optional (14, 23, 24); 6 + 8 + 3 = 17. The two splits are over different columns and agree. §6.1's subsections run §6.1.1 to §6.1.17 and give the same count a third time from a different part of the document. THE SPLIT IS DERIVED IN CODE from the transcribed presence cells rather than typed — klv_security_codec.REQUIRED_TAGS, CONTEXT_TAGS and OPTIONAL_TAGS are comprehensions over ELEMENTS — so a mistyped presence cell moves a count instead of hiding in one.

the_absent_tags_15_to_21.what_the_table_shows: Table 2 carries no row between tag 14 and tag 22. Seven tag numbers are absent and the document draws no row, no placeholder and no note for them.
the_absent_tags_15_to_21.the_revision_history_sentence_that_remov: ST 0102.12's Revision History, the single row 'ST 0102.12 06/22/2017', carries two bullets that describe the removal: 'Eliminated linking of security set to transport stream, elementary stream and individual metadata items' and 'Deleted keys: UMID, Stream ID, Transport Stream ID, Item Designator'. Appendix A corroborates them from the requirement side: `ST 0102.10-32` through `-48` are the deprecated linking requirements and they name exactly those four carriers.
the_absent_tags_15_to_21.WHAT THIS ACCOUNT DOES NOT COVER, AND IT: FOUR KEYS ARE NAMED AND SEVEN TAG NUMBERS ARE ABSENT, so the sentence does not account for the gap. And the document nowhere prints the tag number any deleted key occupied — the revision history names keys, Appendix A names requirements, and neither names a tag. MISB ST 0102.11 would settle which numbers those keys held and IS NOT HELD; it is not a delegation the profile makes and no park stands on it. So this record says the seven are absent, quotes what the document says was removed, and stops. A decoder meeting tag 15..21 on a wire treats it as a tag Table 2 does not draw a row for and carries its octets.
the_absent_tags_15_to_21.what_the_codec_does_with_them: klv_security_codec.ABSENT_TAGS records the seven and ABSENT_TAGS_BASIS carries this whole reasoning; an element with such a tag is refused as `tag_not_in_table_2` with its octets parked.

tag_table_st_0102_12.columns_as_the_document_defines_them: Tag, Name, Data Type or References, Allowed Values or References, Length (Bytes), Required/Optional/Context — the six columns Table 2 draws, and the document defines two of them in the prose immediately above Table 1 (§6.6), which governs Table 2 as well because the two tables list the same elements. LENGTH: 'SMPTE ST 335 [19] defines the length values of metadata items as “stated” as opposed to “normative”. Certain data types may have a flexible length. The value within the Length column in Table 1 specifies either a stated or “Variable” number of bytes. When the value is “Variable”, the length is determined by parsing the encoded BER length as specified in the KLV packet.' PRESENCE: 'Metadata elements are indicated as Required, by Context, or Optional.' THE LENGTH DEFINITION IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS WHY THE CODEC REFUSES RATHER THAN TRUNCATES: a stated length is stated, so an element carrying a different count is not an element with extra octets. Also recorded: §6.7 attaches ONE comment to its table, about the key's own history — 'In creating the key for the Security Metadata Local Set in version RP 0102.4, it was necessary to use the DRAFT of SMPTE RP 336M-2007. That draft contained ambiguous information, which led to the incorrect assignment of bytes five and six in the Security Metadata Local Set. The final version of SMPTE RP 336M removed the ambiguity and it became apparent the Security Metadata Local Set Key needed to be updated.' It bears on the KEY and on no row, which is why it is here and not in one.

the_trap_in_this_table.finding: TAGS 2 AND 12 ARE BOTH A uint8 'Country Coding Method' AND THEIR ENUMERATIONS DISAGREE AT SEVEN OF SIXTEEN POSITIONS. 0x03 is 'FIPS 10-4 Two Letter' under tag 2 and 'ISO-3166 Numeric' under tag 12; 0x04 and 0x05 are shifted by one the same way; 0x0A, 0x0B and 0x0C are the three 'Mixed' methods under tag 2 and 'Omitted Value' under tag 12; and the sixteenth value is 0x10 'GENC Mixed' under tag 2 against 0x40 'GENC AdminSub' under tag 12. Only 0x01, 0x02, 0x06-0x09 and 0x0D-0x0F agree.
the_trap_in_this_table.why_it_is_a_finding_and_not_an_extractio: THE PROSE STATES THE SAME ASYMMETRY INDEPENDENTLY. §6.1.2, of the tag 2 method: 'GENC administrative subdivision codes are not applicable.' §6.1.12, of the tag 12 method: '... and GENC two-letter, three-letter, three-digit numeric or administrative subdivisions.' Two sentences in two sections say what the 0x40 row says, so the divergence survives any doubt about the table extraction.
the_trap_in_this_table.what_it_would_cost_a_decoder_that_missed: A decoder sharing one enumeration between the two elements reports a coding method the packet did not state, for seven of the sixteen legal values, with no error and no clue — the plausible-looking lie this repository's ellipsoid audit exists for, in a new place. klv_security_codec keeps COUNTRY_CODING_METHOD and OBJECT_COUNTRY_CODING_METHOD as two dicts and states the reason at THE_TWO_COUNTRY_CODING_ENUMERATIONS_DIFFER.
the_trap_in_this_table.it_meets_the_documents_own_example: §6.9's worked value is 'a Tag 2 value of “0C”', which is 'STANAG 1059 Mixed' in tag 2's enumeration and 'Omitted Value' in tag 12's — so the only element value the document prints lands squarely inside the divergence.

the_rules_around_the_table.6_2_repetition_rate: §6.2 Security Metadata Repetition Rate. `ST 0102.10-49`: 'A Security Metadata set shall be repeated / updated whenever classification, special handling instructions, releasability, or other mandatory fields change value.' `ST 0102.10-50`: 'Security Metadata Sets shall be repeated no less than every thirty (30) seconds.' Followed by: 'Applications producing short Motion Imagery Data clips or segments of a few seconds in duration may need to repeat Security Metadata Sets as often as every frame.' BOTH ARE OBLIGATIONS ON A PRODUCER ACROSS PACKETS. This adapter states in its own docstring that no state crosses a packet boundary, so it neither checks nor enforces them and says so rather than implying compliance
the_rules_around_the_table.6_3_unclassified_motion_imagery_data: §6.3 Unclassified Motion Imagery Data. `ST 0102.10-54`: 'Unclassified Motion Imagery Data shall be marked with Security Metadata.' `ST 0102.10-51`: 'When Motion Imagery Data is unclassified, the Security Metadata Set value shall be "UNCLASSIFIED//" for Security Classification.' Followed by: 'Other entries in the set which limit or clarify the classification are optional.' WHAT THIS DECIDES HERE: unclassified is a MARKED state with a value on the wire (0x01 by §6.8.1), which is what makes §6.5's absent set a different thing from it. It is also why the complete-set fixture uses 0x01: it is the document's own value for the one classification the document itself names in prose
the_rules_around_the_table.6_4_partial_sets: §6.4 Partial Security Metadata Universal and Local Sets: 'For some operational situations or applications not all metadata elements in Section 6.1 may be required. The originator and his cognizant Security official are responsible to ensure all appropriate security entries are populated.' SO A SET MISSING A `Required` ELEMENT IS NOT MALFORMED. The Table 2 column reading Required states the element's status in a COMPLETE set, and §6.4 says which sets must be complete is decided outside this document by a person. A decoder that refused a partial set would be enforcing a rule ST 0102.12 explicitly declines to state — so a partial set decodes, and which elements arrived is reported rather than judged
the_rules_around_the_table.6_5_absence_of_sets: §6.5 Absence of Security Metadata Universal or Local Sets: 'The proper insertion/extraction of Security Metadata sets into/from Motion Imagery is the responsibility of system developers. Bit stream originators and system developers are responsible to incorporate continual checks for Security Metadata in their applications. THE ABSENCE OF SECURITY METADATA DOES NOT SIGNIFY MOTION IMAGERY DATA AS UNCLASSIFIED.' (Capitals this record's; the sentence is the document's.) WHAT IT DECIDES: a packet with no item 48 is UNLABELLED, and unlabelled is not a value. No classification field is emitted for such a packet — not 'UNCLASSIFIED', not null-meaning-unclassified, not a default. What IS emitted is this sentence, so that a consumer reading the object meets the document's own statement of what the absence does not mean rather than inferring one
the_rules_around_the_table.6_8_conversion_between_universal_and_loc: §6.8 Conversion of Security Metadata Elements between Universal and Local Sets: 'For bandwidth efficiency, some elements in the Local Set are formatted differently than the Universal Set equivalent. This section provides conversion information for the differing items.' §6.8.1 Security Classification, §6.8.2 Classifying Country and Releasing Instructions Country Code and §6.8.3 Object Country Coding Method each state the same pair: 'From Universal Set to Local Set: Convert string to corresponding unsigned integer. From Local Set to Universal Set: Convert unsigned integer to corresponding uppercase string.' THREE SUBSECTIONS FOR THREE ELEMENTS, and they are exactly tags 1, 2 and 12 — the three rows whose Local Set Data Type is uint8. That is where this module's labels come from, and it is why producing one is CARRYING a string the document states rather than naming a number
the_rules_around_the_table.6_9_mixed_country_coding_method: §6.9 “Mixed” Country Coding Method. `ST 0102.10-58`: 'The Mixed Country Coding Method shall be used to support di- or tri-graphs (but not both) from GEC, ISO 3166, GENC and STANAG 1059, respectively, and approved tetragraphs in the same field.' Its example is the document's only printed element value: 'For example, a Tag 2 value of “0C” would indicated the payload of Tag 6 consists of STANAG 1059 di-graphs or tri-graphs (but not both), and one or more tetragraphs from the CAPCO Authorized Classification and Control Marking Register.' (The document's own 'indicated' is preserved.) Note 0x0C is `STANAG 1059 Mixed` in TAG 2's enumeration and `Omitted Value` in tag 12's, which is the divergence above meeting the document's own example
the_rules_around_the_table.and_this_is_what_the_output_shape_was_DE: THE SHAPE WAS NOT DECIDED BEFORE THESE WERE READ, AND THE ORDER MATTERS. §6.5 is what makes an absent set a STATEMENT rather than a gap, so the adapter emits no marking and quotes the sentence; §6.3 is what makes that precise, because it puts a VALUE on the wire for unclassified data (0x01 by §6.8.1) and therefore makes 'unclassified' and 'unlabelled' two different states; §6.4 is what makes a set missing Required elements legitimate, so the codec reports which arrived instead of refusing; and §6.4 with §6.5 together are what make refusing ONE element safe, because the gap a refusal leaves is a shape the document admits and cannot be read as a claim. §6.2 reaches no decode at all and is recorded as reaching none. §6.8 is where the three uint8 labels come from and is the reason producing one is CARRYING a string rather than naming a number.

tag_table_st_0102_12.the_external_code_lists_ruling: GENC (NGA.STND.0033_3.0.1, ref [6]), the GEC register (ref [8]), ISO 3166-1 and -2:2013 (refs [15] [16]), STANAG 1059 Ed 8 (ref [17]) and IETF RFC 2781 (ref [26]) are the code lists and encodings ST 0102.12's country elements are written against. **NONE IS HELD BY THIS REPOSITORY.** THE RULING: this codec CARRIES a country code as the element's own Data Type cell says to carry it and DOES NOT VALIDATE it against a list it cannot read. A decoder that rejected '//XX' because no held file lists XX would be refusing a value on the authority of a document nobody here has opened; one that accepted it while claiming conformance would be worse. So the code is carried verbatim, the coding METHOD the packet declared is carried beside it, and what the code denotes is the consumer's lookup. This is a RULING and not an omission — the same shape as klv_codec's refusal to enforce X.690's 126-octet ceiling from an informative annex quoting an unheld standard
tag_table_st_0102_12.st_336_conformance_and_KLV_11: `ST 0102.12-65`: 'The Security Metadata Universal Set shall conform to SMPTE ST 336 KLV encoding rules.' `ST 0102.12-66`: 'The Security Metadata Local Set shall conform to SMPTE ST 336 [3] KLV encoding rules.' Reference [3] is 'SMPTE ST 336:2007', a DIFFERENT edition from the ST 336:2017 MISP-2019.1 pins — register entry KLV 11. **RESOLVED 2026-09-03, SHAPE (a), AND CITED HERE RATHER THAN RE-ARGUED:** both editions are held and were read against each other clause by clause, and the two differences that reach a key form, a length octet or a UL structure reach no octet a conforming stream can carry. So this module's use of `klv_codec` — which is written against ST 336:2017 and ST 0107.3 — satisfies -66 as well

where_the_item_layer_lives_and_why.module: packages/cdm/synapse_cdm/adapters/klv_security_codec.py — ITS OWN MODULE, beside klv_uas_codec rather than inside it.
where_the_item_layer_lives_and_why.the_precedent_applied: klv_uas_codec's module docstring states where a tag table lives: 'the tag table lives here, one layer up, on the cat048_codec / asterix_cat048 precedent: a codec that reads octets, and above it a codec that knows what they mean.' The precedent is ONE ITEM LAYER PER DOCUMENT — klv_uas_codec cites ST 0601.14a and EG 0601.1 by SHA-256 at module scope so that 'which copy is this read from' has one answer.
where_the_item_layer_lives_and_why.and_the_decisive_argument_is_mechanical: THE TAG NUMBERS COLLIDE AND THE TABLE IS KEYED ON THE TAG. In ST 0601.14a tag 1 is Checksum, tag 2 is Precision Time Stamp, tag 3 is Mission ID, tag 13 is Sensor Latitude, tag 22 is Target Width. In ST 0102.12 they are Security Classification, the Country Coding Method, Classifying Country, Object Country Codes and Version. EVERY ONE OF THIS DOCUMENT'S SEVENTEEN TAGS COLLIDES WITH A TAG OF THAT ONE. Two tables cannot share one dict[int, ...], and a module holding two dicts keyed on the same integers is a module where a lookup's meaning depends on which document the reader thought they were in. Recorded because the choice was between two defensible layouts and this is what settled it.
where_the_item_layer_lives_and_why.what_klv_uas_codec_gained_instead: A second, differently-grounded table: NESTED_SETS = {48: 'MISB ST 0102.12 Security Metadata Local Set'}. ITEMS answers 'what does this integer mean' and stays at the 26 witnessed items exactly as its docstring says; NESTED_SETS answers 'which document's item layer owns these octets'. WITNESSED_TAGS is unchanged at 26 and the scope contract's sentence is untouched.
where_the_item_layer_lives_and_why.and_the_scope_contract_is_CROSSED_HERE_W: Item 48 is NOT in the pinned stream, so klv_uas_codec's scope contract applies to it and crossing it needs an argument. THE ARGUMENT: the contract's reason is that an unwitnessed item's decoder 'could only ever be checked against a fixture written from the same reading of the same table', and item 48's is checked against a SECOND DOCUMENT — ST 0601.14a §8.48 prints KLV Key 06.0E.2B.34.02.03.01.01.0E.01.03.03.02.00.00.00 (CRC 40980) and ST 0102.12 §6.7 registers the Security Metadata Local Set under the same sixteen octets and the same CRC. Two documents, obtained on different days by different routes, in agreement. NO OTHER UNWITNESSED ST 0601 ITEM HAS A SECOND DOCUMENT BEHIND IT, which is why the other 115 rows stay `not yet` and this one does not. WHAT IS STILL TRUE: the pinned stream carries no security set, so nothing in the element layer is checked against an octet anybody has met on a wire.

tag_table_st_0102_12.check_against_the_documents_own_examples: ST 0102.12 PRINTS NO WORKED EXAMPLE OF AN ELEMENT OR A SET, and this was derived rather than assumed: every run of four or more hex pairs in the eighteen pages was extracted and every one is a 16-byte Universal Label — the two registered set keys and Table 1's Universal Set constituent keys. The document's ONLY examples are 'Example of Country Coding Method: GENC Two Letter' (§6.1.2, p.5), 'Example of classifying country: //CZE (Example of GENC code) //GB (Example of ISO-3166 code)' (§6.1.3, p.5) and 'a Tag 2 value of “0C”' (§6.9, p.15). AND THE DELEGATING DOCUMENT SUPPLIES NONE EITHER: ST 0601.14a §8.48's Example KLV Item row reads Tag 30, Len '-', Value 'N/A'. So the strongest check klv_uas_codec has — 26 of 26 decoded values agreeing with the document's own printed Software Values — HAS NO ANALOGUE HERE AND IS NOT SIMULATED. The transcription is checked four ways and no decoded VALUE is checked against the document at all. That is a weaker arrangement than park 1's and this clause exists so that a reader meets the weakness here rather than inferring strength from the shape of the node. A FURTHER NOTE ON §6.1.2 AND §6.1.3: their two examples do NOT pair — 'GENC Two Letter' against a three-letter //CZE — because they are independent examples in two sections and not one worked set, so a fixture combining them verbatim would be internally incoherent. Each fixture pairs a document code with a coding method of the matching width instead.

requirement_ids.how_many: SIXTY-SIX, each occurring exactly once in the document, numbered 1 through 66 with no gap and no duplicate — which is the positive control the numbering offers about itself. Grouped by the version each names: ST 0102.10 sixty-two, ST 0102.11 two (-63, -64), ST 0102.12 two (-65, -66). That grouping matches delegated_specifications_held.st_0102_12.verification_performed, derived independently this round from normalised text.
requirement_ids.live_and_deprecated: THIRTY-EIGHT LIVE and TWENTY-EIGHT DEPRECATED, split by position against 'Appendix A Deprecated Requirements'. AND THE REVISION HISTORY'S OWN LIST IS SHORTER THAN THE APPENDIX, WHICH IS WORTH STATING: it reads 'Deprecated REQ's: 1, 12, 28 through 48, 52, 53' — TWENTY-FIVE — while Appendix A carries TWENTY-EIGHT. The three extra are -18, -19 and -20, the Releasing Instructions ordering rules, which were therefore deprecated by an EARLIER edition. The revision history lists what THIS edition deprecated; the appendix holds everything deprecated by any edition, and reading either as the other gives a count that is wrong by three.

each_one_and_where_it_lands.what_the_four_landings_mean: 'a codec rule' — the requirement is discharged or bounded by code in klv_security_codec or klv_codec. 'a row' — it is what makes a column of `items` below read the way it does, typically the Required/Context marking. 'a fixture' — a fixture exercises the shape it describes, whether or not the codec enforces it. 'not this repository's' — it is an obligation on a PRODUCER of Motion Imagery Data, or it needs a document not held, and the note says which.

ST 0102.10-02.note: 'All security metadata shall be expressed in accordance with MISB ST 0107 [9].' Lands on klv_security_codec's uint16 decode being big-endian and on the BER-OID/BER length walk being klv_codec's, which is ST 0107.3's grammar — the document park 4 closed on. NOTE the delegation is to ST 0107.2 in this document's own reference list [9] and MISP-2019.1 pins ST 0107.3; recorded at delegated_specifications_held.st_0102_12.verification_performed and unchanged by this round.

ST 0102.10-55.note: 'All Motion Imagery Data shall be marked at their proper classification level with appropriate handling, caveats and releasing instructions.' An obligation on a PRODUCER of Motion Imagery Data. This repository translates packets somebody else produced and marks nothing.

ST 0102.10-03.note: tag 1's row. 'Motion Imagery Data shall contain the Security Classification metadata element' is what makes tag 1 Required in §6.7's presence column.

ST 0102.10-04.note: tag 2's row, and the source of its Required marking.

ST 0102.10-05.note: tag 3's row, and the source of its Required marking.

ST 0102.10-06.note: tag 4's Context marking: 'When special handling instructions or compartmented information are used' is the condition the Context column names.

ST 0102.10-07.note: 'When used, SCI/SHI digraphs, trigraphs, or compartment names shall be added identifying a single or a combination of special handling instructions.' A rule about which markings a producer selects. The codec carries whatever arrived.

ST 0102.10-08.note: 'A single entry shall be ended with a double forward slash "//".' Exercised by security_local_set_partial_is_carried_as_partial's tag 5 and the complete set's tag 5, both ending '//'. NOT ENFORCED: the codec carries the string and does not police a producer's punctuation, because rejecting a caveat for a missing slash would drop a marking the packet carried.

ST 0102.10-09.note: 'Multiple digraphs, trigraphs, or compartment names shall be separated by a single forward slash "/".' Exercised by the complete set's tag 4, 'SYNTHETIC-SCI-A/SYNTHETIC-SHI-B//'. Carried, not enforced, for the same reason.

ST 0102.10-10.note: 'Multiple digraphs, trigraphs, or compartment names shall be ended with a double forward slash "//".' The same fixture's terminator. Carried, not enforced.

ST 0102.10-11.note: 'Multiple SCI/SHI digraphs, trigraphs, or compartment names shall be concatenated in one metadata element free text [18] entry.' Reference [18] is ISO/IEC 646, which is where tag 4's iso646 decoding rule comes from, and the ONE ENTRY is why the codec returns a single string rather than splitting on the separators -09 and -10 name.

ST 0102.10-14.note: 'The Caveats metadata element shall be used to indicate FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY (FOUO) data.' A producer's obligation about which marking to emit. DELIBERATELY NOT EXERCISED BY ANY FIXTURE: the round's rule is that no fixture carries a real-world marking, and FOUO is one even though this document prints it.

ST 0102.10-16.note: 'Multiple country codes shall be separated by a blank (space – NOT underscore).' Exercised by the complete set's tag 6, 'CZE ZZZ'. Carried and not enforced — the codec does not split, for -17's reason.

ST 0102.10-17.note: 'Multiple country codes shall be concatenated in one Releasing Instructions metadata element.' ONE ENTRY, so the codec returns one string and does not split on the blank -16 names. Splitting would make the decoder's output a list the packet did not send.

ST 0102.11-63.note: 'Systems shall populate the country codes in the Releasing Instructions metadata element in accordance with the security guidelines (national or international) appropriate to their mission.' A producer's obligation against guidelines this repository does not hold.

ST 0102.11-64.note: 'U.S. systems shall populate the country codes ... in accordance with DOD Manual 5200.01 Volume 2.' Reference [12] is not held and is a producer's obligation besides.

ST 0102.10-22.note: 'The Declassification Date metadata element format shall be YYYYMMDD.' Tag 10's Allowed Values cell and its stated Length of 8, which is what the codec's stated-length check enforces. The DIGITS are not validated: a wrong-shaped date is a marking the packet carried and dropping it would lose it.

ST 0102.10-21.note: 'The Classification or Marking System metadata element shall be free text.' Tag 11's iso646 decoding rule.

ST 0102.10-24.note: 'Multiple Object Country Codes shall be separated by a semi-colon ";" (no spaces).' Exercised by the complete set's tag 13 octets. Carried as OCTETS and never split, because tag 13's encoding is RFC 2781's and RFC 2781 is not held.

ST 0102.10-25.note: 'Multiple Object Country Codes shall be concatenated in one Object Country Code metadata element entry.' One entry, so one carried value.

ST 0102.10-26.note: 'The object country code of the geographic region lying under the center of the image frame shall populate the Object Country Code metadata element.' A rule about what a producer puts in the field. Nothing here computes a country from a frame centre — that would be this adapter deciding which state an image is over.

ST 0102.10-27.note: 'The Classification Comments metadata element shall only be used to convey non-essential security-related information.' A producer's obligation about content, unverifiable from octets.

ST 0102.10-56.note: 'The Security Metadata Version shall be included in all Security Metadata Universal and Local Sets utilizing version four (4) of the security metadata or later.' Tag 22's Required marking.

ST 0102.10-57.note: 'When the Security Metadata Version is not found in the Security Metadata, version three (3) shall be assumed.' RECORDED AND DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED: the codec emits a version_absent advisory quoting this clause and does NOT write 3 into the decoded elements, because the packet did not carry it. Exercised by security_local_set_partial_is_carried_as_partial.

ST 0102.10-49.note: 'A Security Metadata set shall be repeated / updated whenever classification ... change value.' An obligation on a producer ACROSS packets. The adapter's own docstring states that no state crosses a packet boundary, so it cannot see the condition and does not claim to check it. Quoted at klv_security_codec.REPETITION_RATE.

ST 0102.10-50.note: 'Security Metadata Sets shall be repeated no less than every thirty (30) seconds.' The same: a decoder meets one packet at a time and cannot see thirty seconds.

ST 0102.10-54.note: 'Unclassified Motion Imagery Data shall be marked with Security Metadata.' A producer's obligation. What it settles HERE is the CONTRAST §6.5 needs: unclassified data is MARKED data, so an unmarked packet is not an unclassified one.

ST 0102.10-51.note: 'When Motion Imagery Data is unclassified, the Security Metadata Set value shall be "UNCLASSIFIED//" for Security Classification.' Together with §6.8.1 this is where the 0x01 label comes from, and it is why the complete-set and minimal fixtures use 0x01: it is the one classification the document itself names in prose.

ST 0102.10-58.note: 'The Mixed Country Coding Method shall be used to support di- or tri-graphs (but not both) from GEC, ISO 3166, GENC and STANAG 1059, respectively, and approved tetragraphs in the same field.' Tags 2 and 12's Mixed enumeration values, and the source of the complete-set fixture's Tag 2 value 0x0C — the only element value the document prints. NOT VALIDATED: the graphs are carried, because the registers they come from are not held.

ST 0102.10-59.note: 'Current and future U.S. systems producing Motion Imagery Data shall adhere to guidance as directed by the Memorandum ... for GENC and ISO-3166 country codes.' A procurement obligation on a producer.

ST 0102.10-60.note: 'All current systems that do not use GENC or ISO-3166 shall use country codes as defined in GENC and ISO-3166 at their next block upgrade.' The same.

ST 0102.10-61.note: 'All current systems that consume Motion Imagery Data shall understand and properly interpret all country coding methods except for GENC Administrative Subdivisions (GENC AdminSub) code.' THE ONE REQUIREMENT IN THIS DOCUMENT ADDRESSED TO A CONSUMER, which is what this repository is. Discharged as far as octets allow: every one of the sixteen values in each element's own enumeration is decoded to the document's own label, and the two enumerations are kept apart — see THE_TWO_COUNTRY_CODING_ENUMERATIONS_DIFFER. NOT discharged as far as CODE LISTS go: interpreting the code a method names requires GENC, ISO 3166, the GEC register or STANAG 1059, none of which is held, and that limit is ruled at EXTERNAL_CODE_LISTS_NOT_HELD rather than left as a silence.

ST 0102.10-62.note: 'All current systems that consume Motion Imagery Data shall understand and properly interpret at least the country code portion of a GENC Administrative Subdivisions (GENC AdSub) code.' The AdminSub value 0x40 is in tag 12's enumeration and decodes to its label; splitting an AdSub code into its country portion needs GENC, which is not held, so the code is carried whole. The same ruling.

ST 0102.12-65.note: 'The Security Metadata Universal Set shall conform to SMPTE ST 336 KLV encoding rules.' The UNIVERSAL SET is out of this round's scope by ST 0601.14-31, so this requirement governs a carrier nothing here reads. Its edition question is KLV 11's and is resolved — see -66.

ST 0102.12-66.note: 'The Security Metadata Local Set shall conform to SMPTE ST 336 [3] KLV encoding rules.' Discharged by the walk being klv_codec's BER-OID and BER length primitives. THE EDITION QUESTION IS SETTLED AND CITED RATHER THAN RE-ARGUED: ref [3] is ST 336:2007 where MISP-2019.1 pins ST 336:2017, and ambiguity_register KLV 11 RESOLVED it on 2026-09-03, shape (a) — both editions held, read against each other, and the two differences that reach a key form, a length octet or a UL structure reach no octet a conforming stream can carry.
