items.name: Security Classification
items.allowed_values_or_references: UNCLASSIFIED// (0x01) RESTRICTED// (0x02) CONFIDENTIAL// (0x03) SECRET// (0x04) TOP SECRET// (0x05)
items.element_definition_verbatim: The Security Classification metadata element represents the overall security classification of the Motion Imagery Data in accordance with U.S. and NATO classification guidance. Values allowed include: TOP SECRET, SECRET, CONFIDENTIAL, RESTRICTED, and UNCLASSIFIED (all caps) followed by a double forward slash “//”. This is a mandatory entry in a Security Metadata set.

items.name: Classifying Country and Releasing Instructions Country Coding Method
items.allowed_values_or_references: ISO-3166 Two Letter (0x01) ISO-3166 Three Letter (0x02) FIPS 10-4 Two Letter (0x03) FIPS 10-4 Four Letter (0x04) ISO-3166 Numeric (0x05) 1059 Two Letter (0x06) 1059 Three Letter (0x07) Omitted Value (0x08) Omitted Value (0x09) FIPS 10-4 Mixed (0x0A) ISO 3166 Mixed (0x0B) STANAG 1059 Mixed (0x0C) GENC Two Letter (0x0D) GENC Three Letter (0x0E) GENC Numeric (0x0F) GENC Mixed (0x10)
items.element_definition_verbatim: This metadata element identifies the country coding method for the Classifying Country (Par. 6.1.3) and Releasing Instructions (Par. 6.1.6) metadata. The Country Coding Method value allows GEC two-letter or four-letter alphabetic country code (legacy systems only); ISO-3166 [15] [16] two-letter, three-letter, or three-digit numeric; STANAG 1059 [17] two-letter or three-letter codes; and GENC two-letter, three-letter or three-digit numeric. GENC administrative subdivision codes are not applicable.

items.name: Classifying Country
items.data_type_or_references: Text from the appropriate standard preceded by ‘//’
items.element_definition_verbatim: The Classifying Country metadata element contains a value for the classifying country code preceded by a double slash "//."

items.name: Security-SCI/SHI information
items.element_definition_verbatim: §6.1.4 is titled 'Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) / Special Handling Instructions (SHI) Information' and states NO descriptive paragraph at all — it is a heading followed directly by six requirements. Recorded as an absence rather than filled in, because a paraphrase of six 'shall' sentences into a definition would be this transcription writing prose the document does not carry.

items.name: Caveats
items.element_definition_verbatim: The Caveats metadata element represents pertinent caveats (or code words) from each category of the appropriate security entity register. Entries in this field may be abbreviated or spelled out as free text [18] entries.

items.name: Releasing Instructions
items.element_definition_verbatim: The Releasing Instructions metadata element contains a list of country codes to indicate the countries to which the Motion Imagery Data is releasable.

items.name: Classified By
items.element_definition_verbatim: The Classified By metadata element identifies the name and type of authority used to classify the Motion Imagery Data. The metadata element is free text and can contain either the original classification authority name and position or personal identifier, or the title of the document or security classification guide used to classify the data.

items.name: Derived From
items.element_definition_verbatim: The Derived From metadata element contains information about the original source of data from which the classification was derived. The metadata element is free text [18].

items.name: Classification Reason
items.element_definition_verbatim: The Classification Reason metadata element contains the reason for classification or a citation from a document. The metadata element is free text [18].

items.name: Declassification Date
items.element_definition_verbatim: The Declassification Date metadata element provides a date when the classified material may be automatically declassified.

items.name: Classification and Marking System
items.element_definition_verbatim: The Classification and Marking System metadata element identifies the classification or marking system used in the Security Metadata set as determined by the appropriate security entity for the country originating the data.

items.name: Object Country Coding Method
items.allowed_values_or_references: ISO-3166 Two Letter (0x01) ISO-3166 Three Letter (0x02) ISO-3166 Numeric (0x03) FIPS 10-4 Two Letter (0x04) FIPS 10-4 Four Letter (0x05) 1059 Two Letter (0x06) 1059 Three Letter (0x07) Omitted Value (0x08) Omitted Value (0x09) Omitted Value (0x0A) Omitted Value (0x0B) Omitted Value (0x0C) GENC Two Letter (0x0D) GENC Three Letter (0x0E) GENC Numeric (0x0F) GENC AdminSub (0x40)
items.element_definition_verbatim: The Object Country Coding Method metadata element identifies the coding method for the Object Country Code (Par. 6.1.13) metadata. This element allows use of GEC two-letter or four-letter alphabetic country code (legacy systems only); ISO-3166 two-letter, three-letter, or three-digit numeric; STANAG 1059 two-letter or three-letter codes; and GENC two-letter, three-letter, three-digit numeric or administrative subdivisions. Use of this element in version 6 of this Standard and later is mandatory. In version 5 and earlier, it was optional; its absence indicates the default GENC two-letter coding method was used in the Object Country Code element. See also Section 6.9.

items.name: Object Country Codes
items.element_definition_verbatim: The Object Country Codes metadata element contains a value identifying the country (or countries), which is the object of the Motion Imagery Data.

items.name: Classification Comments
items.element_definition_verbatim: The Classification Comments metadata element allows for security related comments and format changes necessary in the future. This field may be used in addition to those required by appropriate security entity and is optional.

items.name: Version
items.allowed_values_or_references: Value is version number of this document; e. g. for ST 0102.10, this value is 0x000A
items.element_definition_verbatim: The Version metadata element indicates the version number of MISB ST 0102 referenced.

items.name: Classifying Country and Releasing Instructions Country Coding Method Version Date
items.element_definition_verbatim: This metadata element provides the effective date (promulgation date) of the source (FIPS 10-4, ISO 3166, GENC 2.0, or STANAG 1059) used for the Classifying Country and Releasing Instructions Country Coding Method. As ISO 3166 is updated by dated circulars, not by version revision, the ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD formatted date is used.

items.name: Object Country Coding Method Version Date
items.element_definition_verbatim: The Object Country Coding Method Version Date metadata element is the effective date (promulgation date) of the source (FIPS 10-4, ISO 3166, GENC 2.0, or STANAG 1059) used for the Object Country Coding Method. As ISO 3166 is updated by dated circulars, not by version revision, the ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD formatted date is used.

what_ST_0102_12_settles_that_the_profile.the_profile_names_the_obligation_and_not: MISP-2019.1's `MISP-2015.1-73` reads 'Motion Imagery shall include Security Metadata in accordance with MISB ST 0102 [55]' and §4.4.2.9 calls the practices 'mandatory for all Motion Imagery Data'. Neither names a tag, a length, a coding method or a classification value. Seventeen elements, six of them Required, are what the delegated document adds — which is the same relation park 1 found between the profile and ST 0601.14.

KLV_7_IS_NARROWED_AND_STAYS_REGISTERED.the_question: The paragraph and the requirement do not use the same term. §4.4.2.9 says 'Motion Imagery Data', which Appendix E defines as 'Three components: Motion Imagery ..., Metadata and/or Audio'; `MISP-2015.1-73` says 'Motion Imagery', which Appendix E defines as a sequence of pictures. So the paragraph's scope includes a metadata stream and the requirement's is the imagery — which decides whether this adapter's input must be labelled at all.
KLV_7_IS_NARROWED_AND_STAYS_REGISTERED.WHAT ST 0102.12 SETTLES: THE DELEGATED DOCUMENT USES THE WIDER TERM THROUGHOUT AND NEVER THE NARROWER ONE. Its §1 Scope is 'marking Motion Imagery Data'; §3 defines Motion Imagery Data the same way Appendix E does, 'Three components: Motion Imagery, Metadata and/or Audio (see MISP)'; and EVERY live marking requirement in it takes the wide term — ST 0102.10-55 'All Motion Imagery Data shall be marked at their proper classification level', -03, -04, -05, -23 'Motion Imagery Data shall contain the ... metadata element', -54 'Unclassified Motion Imagery Data shall be marked with Security Metadata'. The one requirement that named a narrower carrier — -01, 'All MPEG-2 transport streams or files shall be tagged' — IS DEPRECATED by this edition. Derived by reading every live requirement's subject, not by sampling.
KLV_7_IS_NARROWED_AND_STAYS_REGISTERED.WHY IT IS NOT RESOLVED: BECAUSE THE QUESTION IS ABOUT TWO SENTENCES OF MISP-2019.1 AND A THIRD DOCUMENT CANNOT ADJUDICATE THEM. `MISP-2015.1-73`'s own text still reads 'Motion Imagery shall include Security Metadata', the profile still defines that term as a sequence of pictures in its own Appendix E, and ST 0102.12 nowhere quotes or restates -73 — it cannot, being eighteen months older than MISP-2019.1 and delegated TO rather than FROM. A document consistently using the wider term is evidence about what the delegation MEANS and is not the profile's requirement changing its words. Resolving it on the strength of the delegated document's usage would be the move register entry KLV 11 refused when a majority of reference lists named one ST 336 edition: a count elsewhere does not relieve a reader of the sentence in front of them. THE SENTENCE THAT KEEPS IT OPEN, quoted: MISP-2019.1 `MISP-2015.1-73`, 'Motion Imagery shall include Security Metadata in accordance with MISB ST 0102 [55]'.
KLV_7_IS_NARROWED_AND_STAYS_REGISTERED.AND WHAT IS NEW IS THAT THE QUESTION IS: This is the round's actual contribution to KLV 7 and it is worth more than a resolution would have been. §6.5 makes the adapter's behaviour THE SAME UNDER BOTH READINGS: whether or not a standalone metadata stream was required to be labelled, an unlabelled packet is not an unclassified one, so the adapter emits no marking and quotes §6.5 either way. Under the narrow reading a packet with no item 48 may be conformant; under the wide reading it may not be; and in neither case may this adapter say anything about the data's classification. So KLV 7 bounds a CONFORMANCE claim about somebody else's producer and bounds nothing this repository emits — which is why it can stay open without blocking a row, and why park 2 could close over it.

what_ST_0102_12_settles_that_the_profile.what_it_does_NOT_settle: What a country code MEANS. See the_external_code_lists_ruling. And it does not settle the ST 0601 side of anything: all 115 unwitnessed ST 0601 rows still read `not yet` and item 48 is the only one that moved.

security_basis_ruling.no_consumer_ever_received_the_shape_this: AND THIS IS WHY THE ROUND IS SAFE RATHER THAN MERELY CAREFUL. `adapters/klv_security_codec.py` and `attributes.security_metadata_basis` DO NOT EXIST AT TAG v1.4.1 — `git ls-tree v1.4.1` over this package's `adapters/` directory lists no security codec, and `git show` of `adapters/stanag4609.py` at that tag, grepped for `security_metadata_basis`, counts 0. security_basis_ruling.the_precedent_and_its_measured_scale: `klv_uas_codec.LENGTH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY`, shipped in 1.2.0, is the precedent for a policy that rides on every object: four keys — `policy`, `stated_on_every_object`, `defects`, `advisories` — measuring 299 bytes as compact UTF-8 JSON when both arrays are empty. Measured in the same goldens on the same day it is 299 clean, 818 with one advisory and 1 622 with one defect, because its per-instance annotations carry their own prose. THE RESHAPED BASIS LANDS AT THE SAME THREE SCALES: 486 clean, 1 106 with one advisory, 1 773 with one refusal. THAT SYMMETRY IS THE SCOPE RULING OF THIS ACT, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED — the ruling's target is the STANDING keys that rode on every Entity, and the per-instance `refusals[].clause` and `advisories[].basis` fields are left as the named precedent leaves its own `defects[].factual_basis` and `defects[].normative_basis`: they fire on 2 of 34 goldens rather than on all 34, and cutting them would depart from the precedent the ruling itself holds up as the scale to reach.

carrier_basis.text: ST 0601.14a §8.48 Tag 48 Security Local Set, Description 'MISB ST 0102 local let Security Metadata items' (the document's own typo for 'local set', preserved), Format 'KLV set', Length 'Variable', Max Length 'Not Limited', Required in LS? 'Optional'. Its two bullets: 'Use the MISB ST 0102 Local Set tags within the MISB ST 0601 item 48' and 'The length field is the size of all MISB ST 0102 metadata items to be packaged within item 48'. Its §8.48.1 Details: 'MISB ST 0102 [14] allows for the use of either Universal Set or Local Set methods. However, to minimize bandwidth when incorporating MISB ST 0102 into an instance of the UAS Datalink LS, the Local Set method is required.' And `ST 0601.14-31`: 'When incorporating the ST 0102 Security Metadata set into an instance of the UAS Datalink Local Set, the ST 0102 format shall use the Local Set format.' §8.48's Example KLV Item row prints Tag 30 (hex for 48), a Len of '-' and a Value of 'N/A' — SO THE DELEGATING DOCUMENT PRINTS NO WORKED EXAMPLE EITHER, and neither of the two documents behind this codec supplies one

confidentiality_ruling.still_in_code_at: stanag4609._security_basis's docstring, where the ruling is now argued rather than emitted
confidentiality_ruling.note: THE RULING IS UNCHANGED IN EVERY TERM. Replaced on the wire by its own NAME, the token 'CARRIED AND NEVER INVENTED' at `klv_security_codec.CONFIDENTIALITY_RULING`. What moved is where the text lives, and nothing else.
confidentiality_ruling.text: CARRIED AND NEVER INVENTED. Every value below is an octet the packet sent, decoded by a rule this repository can cite in a held document, or it is absent. No marking is defaulted, inferred from context, completed from a partial set, or converted to a nearest listed value. Where the CDM has no field for a security element it goes into Entity.attributes AS THE DOCUMENT NAMES IT — which is why the keys below are ST 0102.12's element names and not a CDM vocabulary

external_code_lists.note: THE CODING-METHOD RULING IS UNCHANGED: a country code is carried as its Data Type cell says to carry it and is never validated against a list this repository does not hold. It is no longer restated on every object; it is here, at `tag_table_st_0102_12.the_external_code_lists_ruling`, and in FORMAT_COVERAGE.md's row set.
external_code_lists.text: GENC (NGA.STND.0033_3.0.1, ref [6]), the GEC register (ref [8]), ISO 3166-1 and -2:2013 (refs [15] [16]), STANAG 1059 Ed 8 (ref [17]) and IETF RFC 2781 (ref [26]) are the code lists and encodings ST 0102.12's country elements are written against. **NONE IS HELD BY THIS REPOSITORY.** THE RULING: this codec CARRIES a country code as the element's own Data Type cell says to carry it and DOES NOT VALIDATE it against a list it cannot read. A decoder that rejected '//XX' because no held file lists XX would be refusing a value on the authority of a document nobody here has opened; one that accepted it while claiming conformance would be worse. So the code is carried verbatim, the coding METHOD the packet declared is carried beside it, and what the code denotes is the consumer's lookup. This is a RULING and not an omission — the same shape as klv_codec's refusal to enforce X.690's 126-octet ceiling from an informative annex quoting an unheld standard

st_336_conformance.note: Also at `tag_table_st_0102_12.st_336_conformance_and_KLV_11` and in ambiguity register entry KLV 11, which is where park 8's resolution is argued rather than cited.
st_336_conformance.text: `ST 0102.12-65`: 'The Security Metadata Universal Set shall conform to SMPTE ST 336 KLV encoding rules.' `ST 0102.12-66`: 'The Security Metadata Local Set shall conform to SMPTE ST 336 [3] KLV encoding rules.' Reference [3] is 'SMPTE ST 336:2007', a DIFFERENT edition from the ST 336:2017 MISP-2019.1 pins — register entry KLV 11. **RESOLVED 2026-09-03, SHAPE (a), AND CITED HERE RATHER THAN RE-ARGUED:** both editions are held and were read against each other clause by clause, and the two differences that reach a key form, a length octet or a UL structure reach no octet a conforming stream can carry. So this module's use of `klv_codec` — which is written against ST 336:2017 and ST 0107.3 — satisfies -66 as well

repetition_rate.note: §6.2 binds a PRODUCER across packets and reaches no decode, which is why an object that cannot see thirty seconds no longer carries thirty seconds' worth of clause.
repetition_rate.text: §6.2 Security Metadata Repetition Rate. `ST 0102.10-49`: 'A Security Metadata set shall be repeated / updated whenever classification, special handling instructions, releasability, or other mandatory fields change value.' `ST 0102.10-50`: 'Security Metadata Sets shall be repeated no less than every thirty (30) seconds.' Followed by: 'Applications producing short Motion Imagery Data clips or segments of a few seconds in duration may need to repeat Security Metadata Sets as often as every frame.' BOTH ARE OBLIGATIONS ON A PRODUCER ACROSS PACKETS. This adapter states in its own docstring that no state crosses a packet boundary, so it neither checks nor enforces them and says so rather than implying compliance

state.note: THE THREE VARIANTS, ONE PER LINE, EXACTLY AS EMITTED. Each was a token, an em dash and a sentence; the token is what stayed.
state.text:
COMPLETE-ON-REQUIRED — the set carries all six elements §6.7 marks Required
PARTIAL — the set is present and does not carry every element §6.7 marks Required
UNLABELLED — this packet carried no ST 0601 item 48

absence.note: §6.5 quoted. Replaced on the wire by the pointer 'MISB ST 0102.12 §6.5', which the UNLABELLED state always carries and the PARTIAL state carries too.
absence.text: §6.5 Absence of Security Metadata Universal or Local Sets: 'The proper insertion/extraction of Security Metadata sets into/from Motion Imagery is the responsibility of system developers. Bit stream originators and system developers are responsible to incorporate continual checks for Security Metadata in their applications. THE ABSENCE OF SECURITY METADATA DOES NOT SIGNIFY MOTION IMAGERY DATA AS UNCLASSIFIED.' (Capitals this record's; the sentence is the document's.) WHAT IT DECIDES: a packet with no item 48 is UNLABELLED, and unlabelled is not a value. No classification field is emitted for such a packet — not 'UNCLASSIFIED', not null-meaning-unclassified, not a default. What IS emitted is this sentence, so that a consumer reading the object meets the document's own statement of what the absence does not mean rather than inferring one

what_is_NOT_emitted.note: Written inline in `_security_basis`. THE BEHAVIOUR IT DESCRIBES IS UNCHANGED and is now stated in that method's docstring and in `the_closed_set_of_state_tokens`'s UNLABELLED note: no classification, no country code, no coding method, no version, and NO `security_metadata` key at all — not an empty one. §6.3 is the contrast and is in `clauses`.
what_is_NOT_emitted.text: no classification, no country code, no coding method, no version. NOT 'null meaning unclassified' and not an empty security_metadata object: attributes carries NO security_metadata key at all for this packet, because a key present with empty contents is a reader's invitation to treat emptiness as a value. §6.3 is the contrast that makes this precise — an unclassified packet is a MARKED packet whose Security Classification octet is 0x01, so 'unclassified' and 'unlabelled' are two different states and this is the second one

what_the_document_asks_of_a_consumer.note: Written inline in `_security_basis`. §6.5's 'continual checks' sentence; the check is still performed per packet and its result is still exactly what `state` reports.
what_the_document_asks_of_a_consumer.text: §6.5: 'Bit stream originators and system developers are responsible to incorporate continual checks for Security Metadata in their applications.' This adapter performs that check per packet and reports its result; deciding what to do about an unlabelled packet is the consumer's, and it is a decision this object gives them the evidence to make rather than one made here

partial_sets.note: §6.4 quoted. Replaced on the wire by the pointer 'MISB ST 0102.12 §6.4', which both present-set states carry.
partial_sets.text: §6.4 Partial Security Metadata Universal and Local Sets: 'For some operational situations or applications not all metadata elements in Section 6.1 may be required. The originator and his cognizant Security official are responsible to ensure all appropriate security entries are populated.' SO A SET MISSING A `Required` ELEMENT IS NOT MALFORMED. The Table 2 column reading Required states the element's status in a COMPLETE set, and §6.4 says which sets must be complete is decided outside this document by a person. A decoder that refused a partial set would be enforcing a rule ST 0102.12 explicitly declines to state — so a partial set decodes, and which elements arrived is reported rather than judged

absence_clause_still_applies.note: Written inline in `_security_basis`. Its content is WHY 'MISB ST 0102.12 §6.5' is in the PARTIAL state's `clauses` list and not only the UNLABELLED one: §6.5 governs the ELEMENTS a present set does not carry as well as the sets a packet does not carry.
absence_clause_still_applies.text: §6.5 governs the ELEMENTS this set does not carry as well as the sets a packet does not carry: an absent Security Classification inside a present set is unlabelled and not unclassified, for the same reason and by the same sentence

element_refusal_policy.note: THE POLICY IS UNCHANGED — the element is refused and the set is not. It no longer rides on every object; it is still reached PER INSTANCE, because the codec generates it into each entry of `refusals`, which is the precedent's own arrangement for a per-instance annotation.
element_refusal_policy.text: THE ELEMENT IS REFUSED AND THE SET IS NOT. A refused element yields no value, its octets are parked verbatim, and a structured refusal names the clause it failed. The other elements decode. THREE GROUNDS, and the third is this document's own: (1) the ST 0601 length policy already rules that discarding well-formed items over one malformed one destroys the evidence a consumer needs; (2) §6.4 makes a set missing elements a legitimate set, so a set that loses one to a refusal is a shape the document already contemplates; (3) §6.5 makes the resulting gap unambiguous — an absent classification does not read as UNCLASSIFIED, so dropping a malformed Security Classification cannot be mistaken for a claim about the data. WHAT IS NEVER DONE: reinterpreting the octets under another rule, or substituting a value the packet did not carry

unlisted_tags_basis.note: THE ONE ENTRY NOT LIFTED FROM A GOLDEN, because no fixture carries an ST 0102 tag outside Table 2 and so no golden ever held this key. Taken from the emitting expression instead. The incompleteness it records — four deleted keys named against seven absent tag numbers — is unchanged and is also at `tag_table_st_0102_12.the_absent_tags_15_to_21`.
unlisted_tags_basis.text: Table 2 carries no row between tag 14 and tag 22. ST 0102.12's Revision History states what this edition removed — 'Eliminated linking of security set to transport stream, elementary stream and individual metadata items' and 'Deleted keys: UMID, Stream ID, Transport Stream ID, Item Designator' — and Appendix A carries ST 0102.10-32 through -48 as the deprecated linking requirements naming those carriers. THE ACCOUNT IS INCOMPLETE AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH: four keys are named and seven tag numbers are absent, and the document never prints the tag number any deleted key occupied. MISB ST 0102.11 would settle it and is not held

label_basis.note: Rode under EVERY labelled element — tags 1, 2 and 12 — as the same 890 bytes three times. Replaced by `label_clause`, the ONE §6.8 subsection that governs that element: §6.8.1, §6.8.2, §6.8.3. That is STRICTLY MORE than the paragraph carried, at 25 bytes.
label_basis.text: §6.8 Conversion of Security Metadata Elements between Universal and Local Sets: 'For bandwidth efficiency, some elements in the Local Set are formatted differently than the Universal Set equivalent. This section provides conversion information for the differing items.' §6.8.1 Security Classification, §6.8.2 Classifying Country and Releasing Instructions Country Code and §6.8.3 Object Country Coding Method each state the same pair: 'From Universal Set to Local Set: Convert string to corresponding unsigned integer. From Local Set to Universal Set: Convert unsigned integer to corresponding uppercase string.' THREE SUBSECTIONS FOR THREE ELEMENTS, and they are exactly tags 1, 2 and 12 — the three rows whose Local Set Data Type is uint8. That is where this module's labels come from, and it is why producing one is CARRYING a string the document states rather than naming a number

value_is_octets_not_text.note: TAG 13 ONLY. Replaced by `value_form`, that rule's own name — 'carried_octets' — which is the `kind` field of §6.7's row for tag 13. The reason the octets are carried rather than decoded is unchanged and is Act 2's subject: RFC 2781 is not held. NOTE ON THE SOURCE CONSTANT: `text` above is the 536 bytes as EMITTED at acb6295, lifted from a golden. The constant it was generated from has since gained the dated clause Act 2 of this round owed it — see `surface_round_2026_09_04` — so the constant is longer than this record's text, deliberately and in one direction only.
value_is_octets_not_text.text: TAG 13 ONLY. The Data Type cell reads `RFC 2781 [26] [27]`, reference [26] being 'IETF RFC 2781 UTF-16, and encoding of ISO 10646, Feb 2000'. **RFC 2781 IS NOT HELD BY THIS REPOSITORY**, so the octets are CARRIED VERBATIM and no string is produced: decoding UTF-16 requires a byte order, a byte order is what RFC 2781 states, and guessing one would be a rule read off a reference rather than off a document. This is the one element of the seventeen whose row is `not yet`, and the reason is an unheld document rather than unwritten code

_local_set_key_basis.note: Written inline in `_security_metadata`. Replaced by `_local_set_key_clauses`, the two clauses whose agreement is the ground: ['MISB ST 0102.12 §6.7', 'MISB ST 0601.14a §8.48']. The key and its CRC 40980 stay on the wire as the facts they always were, and the key is still recorded as the set's IDENTITY rather than as an octet a conforming item 48 carries.
_local_set_key_basis.text: §6.7's registered key, stated here as the set's IDENTITY. It is NOT an octet this packet carried: inside ST 0601 item 48 the key is not on the wire, because §8.48 makes the item's own length 'the size of all MISB ST 0102 metadata items'. the_measurement.a_reading_that_did_not_reproduce: RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED OVER. The round's brief gave the before-figures as an average of 6 490 and an absent case of 6 222. Six serialisations of the acb6295 goldens were tried — compact, default separators, indent=2 with and without ensure_ascii, the raw on-disk span, and the file-shrink delta — and the absent case reads 6 146, 6 167, 6 191, 6 246, 6 318 and 6 298 respectively, with averages from 6 385 to 6 999. surface_round_2026_09_04.what_this_is: THE SURFACE ROUND OF 2026-09-04, ACT 2, AND IT STOPPED AT ITS OWN STOP RULE. The round was sent to acquire IETF RFC 2781, pin it as this repository pins documents, read the byte-order rule off it and move ST 0102.12's tag 13 row off `not yet`. THE DOCUMENT IS FREE, REACHABLE AND WAS READ. IT IS NOT PINNED. The blocker is not the RFC Editor and is not the document: the RFC Editor offers no PDF for RFC 2781, and every pin gate in this repository is PDF-shaped. Act 1 is unaffected — the two acts were separable by the round's own terms.
surface_round_2026_09_04.act_1_is_not_affected_by_this: STATED FIRST, BECAUSE A STOP IN ONE ACT READS LIKE A STOP IN THE ROUND. Act 1 — the basis brought to the precedent's scale — is complete, its structural diff is clean on all 34 goldens, and its record is at `security_basis_ruling`. This node records only what Act 2 found before it stopped.

framing_ruling_st_0601_14.what_this_is: THE FRAMING RULING, 2026-08-26. Parks 4 and 8 own how a key, a tag and a length are written, and this round asked the pinned copy of ST 0601.14 whether it states those rules itself. It states two of the three and delegates the third, so this node records each rule as ESTABLISHED with its section, or as UNDERIVABLE with the sentence that delegates it - and parks 4 and 8 both STAY OPEN. Nothing here flips a tag_table_st_0601_14 row: all 141 remain 'not yet', because a framing layer says where an item begins and never what it means.
framing_ruling_st_0601_14.the_document_rule_this_round_worked_unde: Where ST 0601.14a's own text and worked examples state a rule completely enough to implement and test against, the rule is recorded as established from the pinned copy with its sections cited. Where a rule exists only by reference to SMPTE ST 336 or MISB ST 0107, it is NOT reconstructed from memory or from third-party sources: it is named as underivable and the park's closure stops there. Partial closure was a permitted outcome and partial closure is what happened - and 'partial' here means the tag half of the framing, not a fraction of a park.
framing_ruling_st_0601_14.how_the_verbatim_quotations_were_obtaine: Every quotation below was read positionally from the PDF's own text runs, line by line, and not from a reader-order dump. These PDFs store text with per-glyph kerning splits, so a naive extraction renders 'BER-OID' as 'BER - OID' and '16-Byte' as '16 - Byte'; the quotations here are the glyph runs joined in x-order within each line's own y, which reproduces the printed line exactly. The same method the tag table transcription used, and the reason it is stated again is that a quotation whose whitespace was repaired by judgement is a quotation with a judgement in it.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The 16-byte Universal Label key of the UAS Datalink Local Set.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: SS 6.2, 'UAS Local Set Universal Label', PDF page 4. Restated by the deprecated ST 0601.8-19 block on PDF page 217.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: The UAS Local Set 16-Byte UL “Key” is registered in MISB ST 0807 [3] as: 06.0E.2B.34.02.0B.01.01.0E.01.03.01.01.00.00.00 (CRC 56773)
established_from_the_pinned_copy.second_statement_verbatim: ST 0601.8-18 (Deprecated) The UAS Datalink Local Set 16-byte Universal Key shall be 06 0E 2B 34 - 02 0B 01 01 - 0E 01 03 01 - 01 00 00 00 (CRC 56773)
established_from_the_pinned_copy.the_crc_is_carried_and_not_recomputed: The document prints a CRC beside every Universal Label it states and never states the polynomial. Recomputing one would need a rule from a registry this repository does not hold, and a check that invents its own algorithm checks the invention. So 56773 is recorded as the document's own value and is not verified.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The packet is a Universal Label key, then the length of the value, then the value; the local set's items live inside the value.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: SS 6.3, 'UAS Datalink LS Packet Structure', PDF page 4, and Figure 1 on PDF page 5.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: Figure 1 illustrates the general structure of a UAS Datalink LS packet. A packet is a combination of a UL Key, the Length of the Value, and the Value. UAS Datalink LS items are encapsulated within the Value portion of the packet.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.figure_1_own_labels: UL Key (UAS Datalink LS) / 16 Bytes Identifier; Length of Value / BER Encoded; Value / UAS Datalink LS items / Variable Length; and beneath them 'BER-OID encoded Tag's', 'BER encoded Length's', 'Variable Length Data'. Read from the figure's own Form XObject text runs, which is why it can be quoted at all.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.what_it_does_not_give: The figure NAMES the length field as BER encoded and never says what BER encoding is. That is the whole of the residue below.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: Local Set tags are BER-OID encoded, one octet for 1 through 127 and two or more above 127.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: SS 7.1, 'UAS Datalink Local Set Items Summary', first bullet, PDF page 12.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: The “Tag” column is the KLV Local Set tag number for the item. The tag is an integer but encoded as a BER-OID value when used. Single-byte tags can represent tag numbers from 1 through 127. Tag numbers greater than 127 use two-bytes (or more).
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: klv_codec.decode_ber_oid and encode_ber_oid, over the established width range, exact inverses by exhaustion over 0..16383.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The BER-OID bit pattern for a two-octet value: a leading continuation bit of 1 on the first octet and 0 on the second, seven payload bits each, fourteen bits of value.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: Figure 67, 'Status BER-OID bit pattern', PDF page 212, and the paragraph immediately beneath it.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.figure_67_own_labels: 'Status' / 'BER-OID' over two boxes labelled 'MSB Byte' and 'LSB Byte'; the MSB box carries a leading '1' and '(7 bits)', the LSB box a leading '0' and '(7 bits)'; the payload bits are numbered 6 5 4 3 2 1 0 under each. Read positionally from the figure's Form XObject.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: After decoding the Weapons Status BER-OID value, a 14-bit value remains.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.why_this_is_the_load_bearing_citation: SS 7.1 states WHERE the width changes and never says HOW a multi-octet BER-OID value is assembled. Figure 67 is the only place in the pinned copy that draws the continuation bit, and the '14-bit value' sentence is the only place that states the resulting capacity. Without them the two-octet form would have been inferred from examples rather than read, and klv_codec.BER_OID_MAX would have been a recollection.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The tag encodings themselves, confirmed by worked example across the whole assigned space.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: The 'Example KLV Item (All Hex)' row of every item section in SS 8, PDF pages 31-217.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.what_was_measured: Every 'Tag Len Value' example row in the document was collected. The tag field takes exactly the values 01 through 7F for tags 1-127 and 8100 through 810D for tags 128-141 - 141 distinct encodings, no gap, no duplicate, and every one of them is what SS 7.1's boundary and Figure 67's bit pattern predict. 0x8100 is 128 and 0x810D is 141.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.why_it_is_evidence_and_not_the_rule: 141 examples cannot state a rule; they can only agree with one. They are recorded because they are the positive control on the reading above: a misunderstanding of the continuation bit would have disagreed with the document at 14 places.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The packet checksum: a running 16-bit summation, its range, its algorithm, and what a receiver does when it fails.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: SS 6.6, 'Packet Checksum and Version Number', PDF pages 11-12; the algorithm again at SS 8.1.1.1 and a worked vector at SS 8.1.1.2, PDF page 31.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: To help prevent erroneous metadata from being presented with the Motion Imagery, a 16-bit checksum is included in every UAS Datalink LS packet as the last item. The checksum is a running 16-bit summation through the entire packet beginning with the 16-byte Local Set Key and ending with the length field of the checksum LS item (see Figure 7).
established_from_the_pinned_copy.algorithm_verbatim: unsigned short bcc_16 ( unsigned char * buff, //Pointer to the first byte in the 16-byte UAS Datalink LS key. unsigned short len ) //Length from 16-byte US key up to 1-byte checksum length. { unsigned short bcc = 0, i; // Initialize Checksum and counter variables. for ( i = 0 ; i < len; i++) bcc += buff[i] << (8 * ((i + 1) % 2)); return bcc; } // end of bcc_16 ()
established_from_the_pinned_copy.worked_vector_verbatim: 64 bits to checksum: 060E 2B34 0200 81BB / 060E + 2B34 = 3142 / + 0200 = 3342 / + 81BB = B4FD <-- Final Checksum
established_from_the_pinned_copy.requirements_verbatim: ST 0601.8-08 All instances of a UAS Datalink LS where the computed checksum is not identical to the included checksum shall be discarded. ST 0601.8-11 All instances of the UAS Datalink LS shall contain as the final item Tag 1, (Checksum).
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: klv_codec.bcc_16, transcribed loop for loop, masked to 16 bits because Python integers do not wrap where an unsigned short does. Checked against the document's own vector rather than against itself: the eight octets 060E2B34020081BB give 0xB4FD.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.the_half_that_is_still_blocked: SS 6.6 defines the checksum's RANGE in terms of 'the length field of the checksum LS item', so finding that end means walking the local set, which means the length grammar. bcc_16 therefore takes the range as an argument exactly as the standard's own C does, and this repository offers nothing that computes it. The algorithm is established; applying it to a real packet is not.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: A Zero-Length Item is a tag followed by a length of zero and no value, and it means the value is now unknown.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: SS 6.5, PDF page 10, and requirements ST 0601.14-32, -33 and -34.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: If a metadata producer needs to “shut-off” an item (i.e. make it immediately Unknown) the producer sends a Zero-Length Item (ZLI) which is a Local Set item with no value (i.e. tag followed by a length of zero, with no value).
established_from_the_pinned_copy.why_a_framing_fact_and_not_a_semantic_on: It is the one item shape where the VALUE is absent rather than opaque, so a walk that assumed every item has at least one value octet would desynchronise on it. Recorded here so that the walk, when it is written, is written knowing it. Not implementable now for the same reason nothing else is: a length of zero still has to be read as a length.

underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.rule: BER length encoding: the short form, the long form, and any constraint on which is permitted where.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.status: UNDERIVABLE FROM THE BYTES IN HAND. This is the residue, and it is the reason parks 4 and 8 do not close.

what_the_pinned_copy_does_say.names_the_two_forms_without_defining_eit: SS 6.3.2, PDF page 6, verbatim: 'A VLP is a group of items represented as length-value pairs with the item's tags suppressed. Lengths in BER short or long form precede each item's value as illustrated in Figure 2.' The same phrase recurs at SS 8.115, SS 8.122, SS 8.138 and SS 8.140, and not once is either form defined.
what_the_pinned_copy_does_say.figure_1_labels_the_field_and_stops: 'Length of Value / BER Encoded' and 'BER encoded Length's'.
what_the_pinned_copy_does_say.the_only_constraint_is_in_deprecated_tex: ST 0601.8-07 (Deprecated), Appendix A, PDF page 218, verbatim: 'All instances of item length fields within a UAS Datalink LS packet shall be BER Short form or BER Long form encoded using the fewest possible bytes in accordance with SMPTE ST 336 [2].' It is marked (Deprecated) in the document's own left column.
what_the_pinned_copy_does_say.the_live_route_is_a_second_delegation: ST 0601.8-03, SS 6.3.1, PDF page 5, verbatim: 'All UAS Datalink LS metadata shall be expressed in accordance with MISB ST 0107 [5].' So the rule was not deleted - it was moved out of ST 0601 and into ST 0107.3, which the revision history states in as many words: 'Deprecated Requirements ST 0601.8-02, -04, -05, -06, and -07 / ST 0107.3 includes these requirements as they apply to all MISB KLV based metadata (not just ST 0601)'.
what_the_pinned_copy_does_say.no_worked_example_reaches_long_form: Every 'Tag Len Value' example row in the document was collected and its length octet read. The distinct length octets are 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, 09, 0B, 0E, 13, 14 and 24. THE LARGEST IS 0x24, which is 36. Not one example exercises long form, and not one even reaches the 127 a short form is usually said to stop at. So the examples are consistent with the familiar rule and cannot establish it: what they show is that a length in that set is written as a single octet equal to the length.

underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.why_the_examples_are_not_enough: A codec built from them would accept lengths 1-9, 11, 14, 19, 20 and 36 and have nothing to say about 10 or 200. That is a lookup table, not a grammar, and shipping it as a length codec would be the reconstruction this round was forbidden wearing an empirical costume.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.who_owns_it: PARK 8, SMPTE ST 336:2017, for the encoding; PARK 4, MISB ST 0107.3, for the formatting rule ST 0601 now routes through. Neither document is held.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_closes_it: Either document. Park 8 is a purchase decision and park 4 is a public download, so park 4 is the cheaper of the two and is the one a next round should take.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.implemented_as: klv_codec.decode_ber_length, encode_ber_length and walk_local_set all exist, are importable, and raise UnderivableFromPinnedCopy carrying this text. A reader who reaches for a length decoder gets the park number and the delegating sentence; a missing name would have given an AttributeError and an invitation to guess.

underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.rule: BER-OID encodings three octets wide and beyond.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.status: UNDERIVABLE. Bounded and small, and named rather than quietly extended.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_the_pinned_copy_does_say: SS 7.1: 'Tag numbers greater than 127 use two-bytes (or more).' SS 8.128's details, PDF page 193: 'Given a Wavelength Record FLP, the Wavelength ID in BER-OID format can be one or more bytes. The BER-OID format is self-describing providing the rules for obtaining the number of bytes for the value.' The document ASSERTS that the format is self-describing and never describes it beyond Figure 67's two octets.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.why_it_is_refused_rather_than_extended: Extending Figure 67's continuation pattern to a third octet is arithmetic anybody can do, which is exactly what makes it the tempting reconstruction. The pinned copy neither states the general rule nor works an example above two octets, and ST 0601's own tag space stops at 142 - so nothing in this standard would ever exercise it and nothing in this standard can settle it.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_it_costs_today: Nothing, for this local set: Table 1's highest tag is 141 and the two-octet form reaches 16383. It costs a future nested set whose own tags run higher, and it is recorded so that round knows the rule was never established rather than assuming it was implemented.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.implemented_as: klv_codec refuses a third continuation octet quoting the offset and naming parks 4 and 8. Fixture tag_third_continuation_octet records the refusal.

underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.rule: Whether a non-minimal BER-OID encoding must be REFUSED on parse.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.status: UNDERIVABLE AS A NORM, DECIDED AS AN IMPLEMENTATION, and the difference is stated rather than blurred.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_the_pinned_copy_does_say: ST 0601.8-06 (Deprecated), PDF page 218, verbatim: 'All instances of item Tags within a UAS Datalink LS packet shall be BER-OID encoded using the fewest possible bytes in accordance with SMPTE ST 336.' The requirement is real, it is in this document, and this document no longer asserts it on its own account - it moved to ST 0107.3 with the other four.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.the_decision: klv_codec.decode_ber_oid REFUSES the one non-minimal two-octet form, a leading 0x80. The reason is that accepting it would make two byte strings denote one tag, and a round trip over an ambiguous encoding is a statement about the codec rather than about the wire. It runs in the same direction as all 141 worked examples.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_is_not_claimed: That refusal is normatively required. The sentence requiring minimality is deprecated in this edition and its live successor is in a document this repository does not hold. If ST 0107.3 turns out to require acceptance, this is the decision that changes.

park_4.document: MISB ST 0107.3, KLV Metadata in Motion Imagery
park_4.what_this_round_established_about_it: That it is now the LIVE route rather than a parallel one. ST 0601.14 deprecated five of its own requirements into ST 0107.3 - ST 0601.8-02, -04, -05, -06 and -07 - and two of those five, -06 and -07, are precisely the tag-minimality and length-encoding rules this round went looking for. So park 4 is not merely 'formatting in motion imagery' as the delegation table has it: it now holds the framing constraints ST 0601 used to state itself.
park_4.why_it_does_not_close: Neither half of the shared exit condition is discharged. The document is not obtained, so it is not pinned, and no row set is written from it. Nothing about this round's reading of a DIFFERENT document changes that.
park_4.what_did_change_and_it_is_not_a_closure: Its pinned version is corroborated by a second document. ST 0601.14a's own reference [5] reads 'MISB ST 0107.3 KLV Metadata in Motion Imagery, Nov 2018', which is exactly what MISP-2019.1's Appendix B ref [14] pins. Two independent documents naming one revision is worth recording and is not worth a park state.

park_8.document: SMPTE ST 336:2017, Data Encoding Protocol Using Key-Length-Value
park_8.what_this_round_established_about_it: The precise size of what it owns, which was previously stated as 'key forms, the 16-byte Universal Label, the length forms' and is now narrower by two thirds. The 16-byte Universal Label of THIS local set is in ST 0601.14 SS 6.2 and needs no ST 336. The BER-OID tag form is in SS 7.1 and Figure 67 and needs no ST 336 for one and two octets. What is left to park 8 is the LENGTH grammar and the third BER-OID octet.
park_8.why_it_does_not_close: It is a purchase decision, the document is not held, and a narrower park is still an open park. Recording that a blocker shrank is not recording that it lifted.
park_8.what_did_change_and_it_is_not_a_closure: Its pinned version is corroborated the same way park 4's is: ST 0601.14a's own reference [2] reads 'SMPTE ST 336:2017 Data Encoding Protocol Using Key-Length-Value', matching MISP-2019.1's Appendix B ref [13] exactly. Worth noting because ST 0102.12's reference [3] pins ST 336:2007 instead - an older edition - which is a divergence between two delegated documents this repository holds, and is registered as KLV 11 below.

the_park_outcome.no_row_flipped: All 141 rows of tag_table_st_0601_14 remain 'not yet' and none of them was eligible to move: a framing rule says where an item begins and a row says what an item means. The round predicted no flips and there were none.
the_park_outcome.no_park_opened_and_none_renumbered: The roster is unchanged at twelve parks, one closed and eleven open, ten of the eleven public downloads and one a purchase. This round obtained no document and therefore had no occasion to change it.

what_was_implemented_and_what_deliberate.module: packages/cdm/synapse_cdm/adapters/klv_codec.py. A codec and NOT an adapter: no Adapter subclass, so no registry entry, no ordinal and no roster row. The framing layer cannot read a local set, and a module that registers as an adapter claims it can.
what_was_implemented_and_what_deliberate.the_injected_clock_seam: NAMED AND NOT BUILT, which is a deviation from the round's protocol and is recorded as one. In this package the clock is a parameter of Adapter.__init__ and codecs never take one - gmtif_codec and cat048_codec are the precedent. Creating an Adapter subclass to hold an unused seam would have claimed an ordinal and a roster row for something that cannot parse a length. The seam is built when there is an adapter to build it on.
what_was_implemented_and_what_deliberate.fixtures: fixtures/klv/framing/, thirteen fixtures and their twins, generated by fixtures/klv/spec/build_fixtures.py, which is the only thing that writes them. They are NOT adapter fixtures and the harness cannot replay one; they live in a subdirectory so that a harness run pointed at fixtures/klv still finds nothing and still fails, which is the state fixtures/klv/README.md describes.
what_was_implemented_and_what_deliberate.fixture_identities: UUID-v8 in the f1c7 namespace, identifying the FIXTURE and not anything in it, because a framing fixture's payload carries no identifiers at all.
what_was_implemented_and_what_deliberate.fixtures_omitted_and_why: Three classes, omitted rather than guessed, per the round's own rule that a fixture needing a rule this round could not establish is named in the residue: every length fixture including the truncated-length malformation; every key/length/value triple, which needs a length one rule up; and the 16383-to-16384 tag transition, which needs the third BER-OID octet. Writing any of them would have meant writing the rule first, from memory, and then testing this repository's memory against itself.

page_count_method.ruling: Ruled in FORMAT_COVERAGE.md, 'The page count, ruled from what a reader does with the number'. A page count is one term of a pin's identity row and its job is to let someone holding a copy check they hold the same document - which they do by opening it and seeing how many pages it has. So the count is the number of pages the document HAS, which is the page tree; a raw-object scan counts FILE OBJECTS, a different quantity that coincides only when a file has no orphaned page objects and no incremental update.
page_count_method.what_this_record_used_to_say_and_why_it_: It used to read: 'Counted from each PDF's own page tree - occurrences of /Type /Page across raw objects and across every inflated object stream.' CAT034 Phase 1 found the first file where they disagree and recorded the divergence; the harmonisation round ruled for the page tree and rewrote this field. THE COUNTS IN THIS RECORD DID NOT MOVE - both methods give them - so this is a correction to the description of how they were obtained and not to the values.

page_count_method.how_the_2026_08_26_ST_0601_14_count_was_: THE RULED METHOD, by a walker rebuilt for this round because the previous one was written into a scratch directory and did not survive it - which is itself worth recording, since a method that has to be rebuilt is a method whose description in this file is the only thing carrying it forward. It was validated before its answer was trusted, and validated more widely than the last one: run against ALL SEVENTEEN specification PDFs on disk in this repository, it reproduced SIXTEEN recorded counts exactly - 31, 41, 64, 146, 5, 212, 104, 6, 18, 226, 73, 5, 192, 150 and 5, taken from pin records and from FORMAT_COVERAGE.md's rows for the gmti and nits documents, which state their counts nowhere else. page_count_method.the_paginated_text_variant_ruled_2026_09: A SECOND RULED METHOD, FOR A DOCUMENT WHOSE PAGINATION IS ITS OWN RATHER THAN A PDF PAGE TREE'S, and it is placed here beside the /Pages walk rather than in the text-pin ruling because a reader who wants to know how a `pages` value was produced comes to this node for either kind. THE METHOD: count the form feeds (0x0C), count the `[Page N]` footers, and require THREE things to agree — the two counts, and the highest footer number. All three are reported, and a disagreement is a refusal rather than a casting vote, for the same reason the /Pages walk refuses to pick between a page tree and a raw-object scan: two methods that disagree have not produced a number, they have produced a question. WHY THREE TERMS AND NOT TWO: form feeds alone count PAGE BREAKS, which is one fewer than the pages on any document that does not end with one, and one more on any document that does; the footers alone are a count of PAGES THAT PRINT A FOOTER, which silently drops an unfootered final page; and the highest footer number is the document's own arithmetic about itself. The three together cannot all be satisfied by a document this method would miscount. VALIDATED BEFORE IT WAS TRUSTED, on the only paginated text this repository holds, which is the honest statement of its reach: RFC 2781 gives 14 form feeds, 14 `[Page N]` footers numbered 1 through 14 consecutively, and a highest footer number of 14. All three agree at 14 and the pin records 14. Corroborated two ways beyond the agreement: splitting the text on 0x0C gives FIFTEEN segments whose last is exactly `\n`, so there is no unfootered trailing page for the footer count to have dropped, and the footer numbers form the consecutive run 1..14 rather than a set with a gap. THE REACH IS ONE DOCUMENT AND THAT IS SAID RATHER THAN IMPLIED: the /Pages walk was validated against seven documents before it was trusted and this variant against one, because one is how many paginated text documents are held. A second would be a validation and is not available to be one yet.
page_count_method.why_a_text_pin_carries_pages_AT_ALL_rath: BECAUSE THE FIELD'S JOB IS UNCHANGED AND THE DOCUMENT STILL DOES THE THING THE JOB DESCRIBES. `ruling` above derives the page count from what a reader DOES with the number: they open their copy and see how many pages it has. A reader who opens rfc2781.txt sees `[Page 1]` through `[Page 14]` printed by the document itself, so the number is checkable by exactly the act the ruling names. What would have made `pages` wrong here is a text file with NO pagination — a single unbroken stream — and the answer there is that the field would be absent rather than zero, because zero is a count and absence is the truth. RFC 2781 is not that file. See `text_pin_ruling.what_a_text_pin_that_has_no_pagination_would_do`.

not_committed.the_streams_are_not_in_git_either_and_th: ADDED 2026-08-26 BY THE WALK ROUND. fixtures/klv/streams/ holds a real MPEG-2 transport stream (102 004 664 bytes) and the 977-octet KLV extraction taken from it, and NEITHER IS TRACKED. The exclusion is a DIRECTORY rule - `fixtures/klv/streams/` in .gitignore - and not an extension rule, which is the opposite of the choice made for the PDFs above, so the difference is worth stating rather than leaving to inference. revision_suffixes_live_on_six_pages.finding: Every revision suffix in MISP-2019.1 occurs on six of its 73 pages: the Change Log (PDF page 7), Appendix B (PDF pages 63-66), and one stray inside an Appendix A.2 deprecation note (PDF page 62, 'Note: Requirement moved to MISB ST 0605.9'). NOT ONE requirement and not one section of the body - PDF pages 10 to 57 - states a revision of anything.
revision_suffixes_live_on_six_pages.how_it_was_checked: Every match of the pattern (ST|RP|TRM|EG) followed by a four-digit number, a dot and a revision number was located by page across the whole pinned document.
revision_suffixes_live_on_six_pages.consequence: A reader who takes a version from the requirement that mandates a document gets no version at all; a reader who takes one from a later revision has silently changed what the profile requires. So every delegation row states where the VERSION is stated separately from where the document is REQUIRED, and says 'unsuffixed' at the requirement.
revision_suffixes_live_on_six_pages.what_it_bounds: Ambiguity KLV 5 precisely: the six unversioned references are unversioned IN APPENDIX B, which is the one place a version would have been stated. ST 1402 is not among them and the count stays six.
