what_this_phase_did_not_do: No adapter code, no codec, no fixtures, no golden files. Every mapping row in FORMAT_COVERAGE.md says `not yet`, including all 141 ST 0601 rows this round added.

No mapping row was invented for any field whose layout lives in a document not held. That is the whole discipline of this phase, and this round is where it paid: the 141 rows are transcribed from a document in hand, and the nested local sets among them - items 48, 73, 74, 95, 97, 98, 99, 100, 101 and 102 - carry their contents' owner's name instead of their contents.

No gap was opened and no schema field proposed. Item 59, Platform Call Sign, arrives at gap 1 - the CDM's missing canonical name field - as a fourth format, and item 15 arrives at the MSL-versus-HAE distinction `Position.alt_m` already fixes; neither is a new gap.

No fixture was written, and the reason has not changed: a `.klv` payload is a sequence of key/length/value triplets and parks 4 and 8 own how a key and a length are written. Holding the tag table does not make the octets writable. No UUID-v8/f1c7 namespace was allocated and no clock was injected, because there is nothing yet to feed either.

No value in the 141 rows was read from ST 0601.19, and the one item where the two documents differ in meaning - item 42 - carries .14's silence as normative with the divergence recorded as a note beside it.
The parks table was not renumbered and no new park was opened, though ST 0601.14's own reference list names six further documents this repository does not hold. See parks.what_this_round_changed.

The premise that the MISP fixes the Precision Time Stamp's EPOCH was carried into this phase and is FALSE against the pinned profile: `epoch`, `1970`, `microsecond` and `leap` occur zero times in its 73 pages, and the only timescale it names is an example ('such as International Atomic Time (TAI)'). THAT FINDING STANDS AND ITS REACH IS NOW CORRECTED: ST 0601.14, which the profile delegates to and which this round obtained, DOES state the epoch - SS 6.4 and SS 8.2, '1970-01-01T00:00:00Z', SI seconds in microseconds, leap seconds excluded and therefore not UTC. A first draft of this record asserted the opposite, that item 2's section defers the epoch to ST 0603; that was written before SS 8.2 was read and it is wrong. See tag_table_st_0601_14.what_ST_0601_14_settles_that_the_profile_left_open. Park 3 stays open for the reasons recorded there.

length_ruling_st_0107_3.what_this_is: THE LENGTH RULING, 2026-08-26, and the round that discharged the residue the framing ruling named. The framing round asked ST 0601.14a for three framing rules, got two, and recorded the third as UNDERIVABLE with the sentence that delegated it. This round followed that sentence. ST 0601.8-03 - 'All UAS Datalink LS metadata shall be expressed in accordance with MISB ST 0107 [5]' - points at MISB ST 0107.3, six pages, and that document states the length grammar on its own account. PARK 4 IS CLOSED. Park 8 stays OPEN and is narrower again.
length_ruling_st_0107_3.the_document_rule_this_round_worked_unde: Unchanged from the framing round, and it had to be, because the trap inverted. The framing round's hazard was somebody supplying the familiar BER length rule from memory. This round's hazard is that ST 0107.3's rule IS the familiar rule - so a codec written from memory would have passed every test. What separates the two is that every clause below is derived from octets the document prints, and the derivation is written out example by example so a reader can check it against six pages rather than take it. Had ST 0107.3 said something else, the same method would have produced something else.
length_ruling_st_0107_3.the_question_this_round_was_SENT_to_answ: Park 4's half of the length residue, in four parts: the short-form/long-form rule, the long-form length-of-length octet, any stated ceiling on length octets, and any constraint on which form an encoder may emit. The fourth was the one that decided park 4, because 'free choice' and 'minimal encoding required' produce different codecs and the framing round could not tell which ST 0107.3 required.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The short form: for lengths below 128, one octet, and the octet IS the length.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: For example, encoding the length of two (2), a value less than 128, with long form uses two bytes (0x8102) instead of the short form one-byte (0x02) length.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.how_it_is_derived: The document prints 0x02 as the short form of 2 and names 'values less than 128' as the range for which long form is the wasteful choice. So 0..127 is one octet with no flag bit to strip.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The long form: the first octet's low seven bits are the COUNT of following octets, and those octets are the length big-endian.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: SS 6.3.2, PDF page 4, for the form; ST 0107.2-01 and ST 0107.2-02 in SS 6.1, PDF page 2, for the octet order.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: BER is an efficient encoding of a length; however, by either using the long form for values less than 128, or by prepending a long form value with zero-byte values, BER becomes less efficient. For example, encoding the length of two (2), a value less than 128, with long form uses two bytes (0x8102) instead of the short form one-byte (0x02) length. Another example is encoding the value 128 with padded zeros (0x8300 0080) instead of the optimized value with two bytes (0x8180).
established_from_the_pinned_copy.how_it_is_derived: THE DERIVATION WRITTEN OUT, because this is the clause a recollection would have supplied. The passage prints four encodings of two lengths: 0x02 -> 2 short form; 0x81 0x02 -> 2 long form with ONE following octet; 0x81 0x80 -> 128 long form with ONE following octet; 0x83 0x00 0x00 0x80 -> 128 long form with THREE following octets. 0x81 introduces one and 0x83 introduces three, so the low seven bits of the first octet are a count. The document also states how it COUNTS: it calls 0x8180 'two bytes' and 0x8102 'two bytes', so the introducer is included in the total. The following octets are big-endian by ST 0107.2-02, 'Byte order shall be big-endian or MSB'. Two data points plus an octet-order requirement fix the shape uniquely, and nothing is imported from outside the document.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.second_statement_verbatim: ST 0107.3-05 All instances of item Length fields within a MISB defined KLV Universal or Local Set shall be BER Short form or BER Long form encoded using the fewest possible bytes.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: klv_codec.decode_ber_length and encode_ber_length. Fixtures length_long_form_lowest (8180, the document's own), length_long_form_two_octets and length_non_minimal_padded_zeros (83000080, the document's own).

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: Minimal encoding is REQUIRED. An encoder does NOT choose freely between the forms.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: ST 0107.3-05, SS 6.3.2, PDF page 4. LIVE text, not deprecated.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: All instances of item Length fields within a MISB defined KLV Universal or Local Set shall be BER Short form or BER Long form encoded using the fewest possible bytes.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.this_is_the_answer_to_park_4s_question: YES to minimality, NO to free choice. And it is the same sentence ST 0601.14a carries as ST 0601.8-07 with two edits: the onward delegation 'in accordance with SMPTE ST 336 [2]' is REMOVED, and the scope widens from 'a UAS Datalink LS packet' to 'a MISB defined KLV Universal or Local Set'. ST 0601.14a's revision history said the content moved here 'as they apply to all MISB KLV based metadata (not just ST 0601)'; this is the content, and it arrived without the delegation. So the constraint is ST 0107.3's own and does not route onward to park 8.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.what_it_makes_possible: A TOTAL encoder with no form selector. For every length there is exactly one conforming encoding, so encode_ber_length takes the length and nothing else - the ruling is enforced by the signature rather than by a check. test_the_length_codec_is_total_because_st_0107_3_05_leaves_no_choice_of_form asserts the parameter list.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: klv_codec.decode_ber_length refuses both non-minimal forms as KLVFramingError; encode_ber_length cannot express either.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The two non-minimal forms, named and refused: long form for a value below 128, and leading zero octets.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: by either using the long form for values less than 128, or by prepending a long form value with zero-byte values, BER becomes less efficient
established_from_the_pinned_copy.why_exactly_two_and_not_a_general_policy: Because the document names exactly two and works an example against each. A codec refusing 'non-minimal encodings' in general would be enforcing a rule nobody wrote; a codec refusing these two is enforcing SS 6.3.2's sentence. They happen to be exhaustive over the long form - a long-form encoding is minimal iff its value is at least 128 and its leading octet is non-zero - and that they coincide is worth stating rather than relying on.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: Two KLVFramingError branches, each quoting the document's own example against the octets in hand. Fixtures length_non_minimal_long_form (8102) and length_non_minimal_padded_zeros (83000080).

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: A zero length is legal, and the Value is then absent rather than empty.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: The Length defines the number of bytes used by the Value. Lengths are usually positive numbers; however, a zero length is possible in unique cases. Values are the binary representation describing a specific item. In the case of a zero Length, the Value is not a part of the item (see MISB ST 0601 [3]).
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: encode_ber_length(0) is 0x00 and walk_local_set advances past such an item without consuming a value octet. Fixtures length_short_form_zero and item_zero_length.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: The BER-OID chain rule for ANY width, which is the '(or more)' ST 0601.14a SS 7.1 named and never defined.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: BER-OID tags are one or more bytes linked together in chain fashion. In BER-OID a zero in the Most Significant Bit (msb) position terminates the tag's chain. For example, when the msb is set to zero in the first byte, this forms a one-byte tag number ranging from 0x00 to 0x7F. When the msb of the first byte is set to one, the second successive byte becomes part of the BER-OID chain. In continued fashion, if the second byte's msb is set to one, the next byte becomes part of the chain. This pattern continues until the msb of a final byte in the chain is zero. Together the seven Least Signification Bits (lsb) of each byte in the chain form the tag number.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.second_statement_verbatim: Using BER-OID for the tags in all MISB local sets enables efficient tag encoding and unlimited future growth.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.this_was_a_residue_of_the_framing_round_: The framing round recorded 'BER-OID encodings three octets wide and beyond' as UNDERIVABLE and refused a third continuation octet, on the ground that extending Figure 67's pattern was 'arithmetic anybody can do, which is exactly what makes it the tempting reconstruction'. SS 6.3.1 states the general rule, so the extension is now a transcription. decode_ber_oid follows the chain and encode_ber_oid emits any non-negative integer.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.what_this_cost_in_the_codec: BER_OID_MAX_OCTETS is DELETED - a cap beside a codec that no longer honours it is a constant nothing reads. BER_OID_MAX is KEPT at 16383 and re-documented as a waypoint rather than a limit: it is what the delegating document could prove alone, and the exhaustive round-trip test still runs over it because the range fits in a test.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: klv_codec.decode_ber_oid and encode_ber_oid. Fixture tag_three_octet_lowest (818000 -> 16384) REPLACES the refusal fixture tag_third_continuation_octet (818100).

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: Non-minimal BER-OID tags are forbidden, on LIVE authority.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: To prevent BER-OID from including leading zeros, ASN.1 forbids the use of 0x80 in the first byte of a BER-OID value.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.this_is_a_PROMOTION_and_not_a_behaviour_: decode_ber_oid already refused a leading 0x80. The framing round recorded that refusal as 'UNDERIVABLE AS A NORM, DECIDED AS AN IMPLEMENTATION' because the only sentence requiring tag minimality in ST 0601.14a was ST 0601.8-06, marked (Deprecated), and it wrote: 'If ST 0107.3 turns out to require acceptance, this is the decision that changes.' IT DID NOT. ST 0107.3 forbids the octet by name, so the refusal is now transcribed rather than decided. The behaviour is identical and the provenance is not, and the caveat is recorded as discharged rather than deleted.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.one_honest_wrinkle: SS 6.3.1 attributes the prohibition to ASN.1 rather than asserting it as a numbered ST 0107.3 requirement - 'ASN.1 forbids'. So it is live prose in a held document reporting a rule from a document this repository does not hold. That is materially stronger than a deprecated requirement and materially weaker than a 'shall', and it is recorded at that strength rather than rounded up. Registered as KLV 13, which also notes that the reference it points at is X.680.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: klv_codec.decode_ber_oid's leading-0x80 refusal, whose message now quotes SS 6.3.1 and names ST 0601.8-06 as the deprecated predecessor. Fixture tag_non_minimal_two_octets.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: Bit and byte order are big-endian, KLV-wide and retroactively.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: SS 6.1, 'Bit and Byte Order', PDF page 2. NOTE THE PREFIX: these two requirements are numbered ST 0107.2, not ST 0107.3.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: ST 0107.2-01 Bit order shall be big-endian or msb. / ST 0107.2-02 Byte order shall be big-endian or MSB.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.why_the_prefix_is_0107_2: MISB stamps a requirement with the edition that introduced it, and this edition's revision history says it 'Added requirements -03 through -13'. So -01 and -02 came from ST 0107.2 - registry document 4149, which 0107.3 supersedes - and keep their prefix. Citing them as ST 0107.3-01/-02 would cite strings this document does not contain.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.what_it_bears_on: decode_ber_length reads a long-form payload big-endian on ST 0107.2-02's authority, and it is the only octet-order rule in the chain: ST 0601.14a never states one. So the length codec's endianness is cited to a requirement whose number is not this edition's, which is exactly the sort of thing that gets miscited once and then propagates.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: int.from_bytes(payload, 'big') in klv_codec.decode_ber_length, with the requirement quoted at the line.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: A decoder must skip items it does not recognise, using the Length to find the next one.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: Applications which decode MISB KLV Local Sets shall skip unknown Local Set values so as to not impact the decoding of known Local Set items within the same Local Set instance.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.supporting_prose_verbatim: One advantage of KLV is the ability to skip or ignore items which may not be known by a consumer of the data. For example, suppose a new version of a Local Set introduces new tags which an existing decoder does not understand. Instead of crashing, the decoder simply ignores any item it does not understand - this makes a decoder 'future-proof'. In such cases, the Length specified by the Tag is used to skip the correct number of bytes to the next item.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.implemented_as: walk_local_set satisfies it STRUCTURALLY rather than with a skip list: it knows no tags at all, so every item is equally unknown to it and the caller decides what it recognises. The 141-row tag table is in this file and nothing in klv_codec consults it.

established_from_the_pinned_copy.rule: ST 0107.3 is a RESTRICTING profile of SMPTE ST 336, not a deferral to it.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.locus: SS 6.2, 'SMPTE KLV', PDF page 2, and ST 0107.3-03.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.verbatim: The MISB standards define requirements which incur limits on the full SMPTE 336, making the MISB standards a profile of the SMPTE standards.
established_from_the_pinned_copy.second_statement_verbatim: ST 0107.3-03 All Local Set KLV metadata shall be formatted in compliance with SMPTE ST 336 [1].
established_from_the_pinned_copy.why_this_matters_to_park_8: It is the answer to the round's question 'does 0107.3 add any constraint of its own on top of the delegation'. YES, and ST 0107.3-05's minimality is that constraint. Which is why the length codec is COMPLETE AND TOTAL with park 8 still open: the delegation widens what ST 336 would allow and ST 0107.3 narrows it, and the narrowed grammar is fully stated here.

underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.rule: 0x80 as a FIRST LENGTH OCTET - a long form declaring zero following octets.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.status: UNDERIVABLE FROM THE BYTES IN HAND. PARK 8. The one residue in the length grammar and the reason park 8 is not closed by this round.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_the_pinned_copy_does_say: NOTHING, and the silence is the finding. SS 6.3.2 defines the short form and the long form and never mentions a count of zero. In BER this is the INDEFINITE-LENGTH form, whose meaning is SMPTE ST 336's - and naming it as such is already at the edge of what this repository may assert, which is why the codec refuses rather than describing.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.the_delegating_sentence_verbatim: ST 0107.3-03 All Local Set KLV metadata shall be formatted in compliance with SMPTE ST 336 [1].
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.does_0107_3_add_a_constraint_on_top_of_t: NO, not for this octet. It adds ST 0107.3-05's minimality, which bears on every OTHER long form and cannot reach this one: 0x80 encodes no length at all, so 'fewest possible bytes' has nothing to compare. This is the one place in the grammar where the profile's restriction does not cover the delegation's surface.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.why_it_costs_nothing_today: A conforming encoder never emits it - ST 0107.3-05 makes every length's encoding unique and none of them is 0x80 - so the octet is unreachable from any stream this repository would write or any stream a conforming implementation would. It is reachable from a NON-conforming stream, which is exactly why the decoder must say something honest about it.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.implemented_as: klv_codec.decode_ber_length raises UnderivableFromPinnedCopy carrying park 8 and ST 0107.3-03. Fixture length_indefinite_first_octet, whose generator check asserts the exception TYPE so a later round cannot decide what 0x80 means without buying the document.

underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.rule: Any ceiling on the NUMBER of length octets.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.status: NOT STATED BY ST 0107.3. PARK 8, and recorded as an absence that was searched for rather than one that was assumed.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_the_pinned_copy_does_say: SS 6.3.2 states no maximum. The document's only maxima are elsewhere and govern a different quantity: SS 6.3.3 'items may have maximum lengths defined. When encoding a Value do not exceed the maximum limits', and ST 0107.3-07, 'Where a MISB standard defines a numeric maximum Length for a Local Set item's Value, the encoded Value shall not exceed the number of bytes defined by the maximum Length'. Both bound a VALUE's size, not a length field's width. The whole six pages were searched for 'maximum', 'limit', 'ceiling' and the numerals 127 and 128; the only occurrences are those two and SS 6.3.2's own 'values less than 128'.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.the_bound_the_codec_uses_is_STRUCTURAL_a: BER_LENGTH_OF_LENGTH_MAX = 127, because the first octet carries the long-form flag in bit 7 and the count in the remaining seven bits, so 127 is the largest count that octet can express. That is arithmetic on the shape SS 6.3.2's own examples fix, not a citation, and the constant's comment says so. Whether ST 336 imposes a LOWER ceiling is park 8's.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.implemented_as: encode_ber_length raises UnderivableFromPinnedCopy above the structural bound, carrying park 8 and the sentence that states no ceiling. Not KLVFramingError: a caller asking for a 128-octet length field is not handing over wrong bytes, they are asking a question this repository cannot answer.

underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.rule: Whether a DECODER must reject a non-minimal length.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.status: UNDERIVABLE AS A NORM, DECIDED AS AN IMPLEMENTATION - and the decision now rests on live authority, which is the difference from the framing round's version of this same entry.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_the_pinned_copy_does_say: ST 0107.3-05 is a 'shall' on the ENCODING: lengths 'shall be BER Short form or BER Long form encoded using the fewest possible bytes'. It does not say what a reader does when it meets a violation. SS 6.3.2's prose frames the two non-minimal forms as inefficient - 'BER becomes less efficient' - rather than as invalid, which pulls gently the other way.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.the_decision: klv_codec.decode_ber_length REFUSES both, as KLVFramingError - these bytes are wrong - because ST 0107.3-05 says they are wrong, in the live edition ST 0601.14a's live route points at. The second reason is the one the framing round gave for tags: accepting them would make several byte strings denote one length, and a round trip over an ambiguous encoding is a statement about the codec rather than about the wire.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.the_sentence_that_pulls_the_other_way_an: ST 0107.3-04 requires decoders to 'skip unknown Local Set values so as to not impact the decoding of known Local Set items', which is a be-permissive requirement. It is about unknown TAGS, not malformed lengths, and a decoder cannot honour it at all without first reading the length correctly - so a strict length reader is compatible with it. Recorded because the tension is real and an unstated tension reads as an unexamined one.
underivable_from_the_bytes_in_hand.what_is_not_claimed: That refusal is normatively required of a decoder. If a later ST 0107 or ST 336 requires acceptance, this is the decision that changes - and it is the same sentence the framing round wrote about the tag refusal, which is now discharged. This one is not.

park_4.document: MISB ST 0107.3, KLV Metadata in Motion Imagery
park_4.what_discharged_it: BOTH halves of parks.shared_exit_condition, and it needed both. FIRST HALF: the exact version the delegation table pins was obtained - 0107.3, not the current 0107.4 - and pinned in fixtures/klv/spec/ by SHA-256, byte count and page count with its title-page identity read, at delegated_specifications_held.st_0107_3. SECOND HALF: 'the row set that document supports' is written. ST 0107.3 defines no tag table and has no row set to write; what it supports is the FRAMING GRAMMAR, and that is klv_codec.decode_ber_length, encode_ber_length and walk_local_set, which stopped raising this round, plus thirteen new fixtures in fixtures/klv/framing/.
park_4.why_the_second_half_was_not_waived_and_h: Because park 1 was not given that discount and park 2 is still open for exactly this reason - ST 0102.12 has been held since 2026-08-26 and its park stays open on the stated ground that no row set is written from it. So 'the row set that document supports' had to be read for a document that supports no rows. It is read as 'the artefact this document makes writable', which for a field dictionary is a row set and for a framing standard is a codec. park_8.document: SMPTE ST 336:2017, Data Encoding Protocol Using Key-Length-Value

WHAT IS LEFT IS TWO THINGS AND BOTH ARE ABSENCES: 0x80 as a first length octet, which ST 0107.3 never mentions, and any ceiling on the count of length octets, which ST 0107.3 does not state. park_8.the_economics_moved_and_it_is_recorded_n: ST 0107.3 SS 6.3.3.1 names a DIFFERENT source for the length grammar than the parks table does: 'Items using "ber" types in the MISB standards use the ASN.1 [4] Basic Encoding Rules for Lengths rules', where [4] is 'ITU Rec X.680 (08/15)'. NOT ACTED ON, for two reasons: BER's encoding rules are X.690 and not X.680, so the reference itself needs adjudicating (registered as KLV 13), and changing a park's reopen route on the strength of a reference list read in passing is the roster change the park 1 round refused to make.

value_encoding_requirements.what_this_is: The seven ST 0107.3 requirements that govern VALUES rather than framing, transcribed because ST 0107.3 SS 1 makes them retroactive - 'It applies retroactively to all documents approved by the Motion Imagery Standards Board (MISB)' - and because the round that writes a value decoder should not have to fetch this document again. NOTHING IN klv_codec IMPLEMENTS ANY OF THEM.
value_encoding_requirements.ST 0107.3-06: Where a MISB standard defines a numeric required Length for a Local Set item's Value, the encoded Value shall match the number of bytes defined by the required Length.
value_encoding_requirements.ST 0107.3-07: Where a MISB standard defines a numeric maximum Length for a Local Set item's Value, the encoded Value shall not exceed the number of bytes defined by the maximum Length.
value_encoding_requirements.ST 0107.3-08: Where a MISB standard defines a Local Set item with a KLV format of, or prefixed with, 'float,' the encoded Value shall use the IEEE 754-2008 [5] standard to encode the value.
value_encoding_requirements.ST 0107.3-09: Where a MISB standard defines a Local Set item with a KLV format of 'IMAPA' or 'IMAPB,' and the Local Set item allows variable length encoding, the encoded Value shall use the fewest number of bytes, while maintaining system precision.
value_encoding_requirements.ST 0107.3-10: Where a MISB standard defines a Local Set item with a KLV format of, or prefixed with, 'uint' or 'int,' and the Local Set item allows variable length encoding, the encoded value shall remove leading zero or leading sign extension bytes.
value_encoding_requirements.ST 0107.3-11: Where a MISB standard defines a Local Set item with a KLV format of 'ber' and the item allows variable length encoding, the encoded Value shall use the fewest number of bytes.
value_encoding_requirements.ST 0107.3-12: Where a MISB standard defines a Local Set item with a KLV format of 'utf8' and the Value is not the empty string, the encoded value shall have all leading and trailing, null (0x00), tab (0x09), line feed (0x0A), carriage return (0x0D), and space (0x20) characters removed, unless the item definition allows them.
value_encoding_requirements.ST 0107.3-13: Where a MISB standard defines a Local Set item with a KLV format of 'utf8' and the Value is not the empty string, the encoded value shall have all characters in the hex ranges (inclusive) of 0x00 through 0x08, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x0E through 0x1F, and character 0x7F removed, unless the item definition allows them.
value_encoding_requirements.the_empty_string_versus_the_unknown_stri: SS 6.3.3.2, and it is a distinction a value decoder will get wrong once: 'The emptystring uses a single null character (0x00) with no other characters to indicate the string is blank. The length of the emptystring within KLV is one (1), for the null character' and 'A string item with a length of zero (0) signifies an "Unknown" string.' So length 1 holding 0x00 is empty and length 0 is unknown, which are different CDM values and differ by one octet on the wire.
value_encoding_requirements.ST 0107.3-11_is_the_one_that_bears_on_th: It requires 'ber' TYPE VALUES to use the fewest bytes - a Value whose content is a BER length, which is a different thing from the Length field of an item. ST 0107.3-05 is the one that governs the Length field. The two say the same thing about different octets and it would be easy to cite the wrong one.

what_the_walk_measured.how_these_numbers_were_obtained: klv_codec.walk_local_set was pointed at the 977 octets and every value below is its yield. NONE was typed and none was carried from a previous round.
what_the_walk_measured.why_the_checksum_result_is_load_bearing: Not a decoration on a walk that already worked. Six independent 16-bit summations, each over its whole packet from the first octet of the Universal Label to the length octet of the checksum item per SS 6.6, each agreeing with the value the emitter stored. That arithmetic fails if ANY octet in the packet is not what the emitter wrote, so it does two things at once: it confirms the walk's offsets FROM OUTSIDE THE WALK - a mis-parsed length would have put the checksum item's own length octet elsewhere and the range would have been wrong - and it RULES OUT CORRUPTION as an explanation for anything the walk found, in particular for item 22's four octets.
what_the_walk_measured.the_only_other_length_variation: Item 11 carries 3 octets in five packets and 2 in the sixth. It is a utf8 item with a Max Length rather than a Required Length, so the variation is the document's own allowance and not a finding.

the_one_thing_that_does_not_fit.what: Item 22, Target Width, carries FOUR octets where ST 0601.14a SS 8.22 states a Required Length of 2. It does so at all six sites, and the top two octets are 0x0000 at all six - so the value fits the uint16 the document specifies and the excess is two leading zero octets.

act_1_the_self_refutation_test.the_test: An emitter that stamps edition 1 while using items that POSTDATE edition 1 refutes its own stamp. Chosen because it needs no document this repository does not hold. If the held bytes date any of the stream's 26 tags later than edition 1, item 65's 0x01 is an emitter stamp rather than a provenance claim, the declared-edition reading collapses, and item 22 is a stream defect against ST 0601.13-29 with the offsets already in hand.
act_1_the_self_refutation_test.outcome: NOT REFUTED. The held documents do not date the introduction of ANY item at all.
what_was_looked_for_and_is_absent: ST 0601.14a's revision history, SS 4, has THREE rows - ST 0601.14 dated 11/1/2018, ST 0601.14a dated 05/1/2020, and the undeclared 08/19/2021 row that KLV 10 already records. It reaches back no further than edition 14 and names no item's first appearance.

ST 0601.19's revision history has THREE rows too - ST 0601.19 dated 03/02/2023, then 05/10/2024 and 06/11/2025 - and reaches back no further than its own edition. Consulted only as a second sample of the same drafting habit, never as a source of tag semantics, which reconciliation_ruling forbids.

NO ITEM-INTRODUCTION ANNOTATIONS. A search of the 218-page text for 'was added', 'added in ST', 'introduced', 'since ST 0601', 'new in ST', 'prior to ST' and 'starting with ST' returns nothing in any item section.
TABLE 1 HAS NO EDITION COLUMN. SS 7.1 lists its columns itself - Tag, Name, Units, Format, Len, SDCC, MUL, Description - and none of them dates anything.

THE ONE DATING DEVICE THE DOCUMENT CARRIES CANNOT REACH EDITION 1. ST 0601 stamps a requirement with the edition that introduced it, and ST 0601.14a demonstrates the convention in both directions on its own pages: SS 4 says 'Added requirement ST 0601.14-31' and 'Added Requirement ST 0601.14-35' of identifiers carrying .14, and 'Deprecated Requirements ST 0601.8-02, -04, -05, -06, and -07' of identifiers that keep edition 8's number through their deprecation. The document contains 33 DISTINCT REQUIREMENT IDENTIFIERS spanning exactly FIVE editions - 8, 9, 10, 13 and 14 - and NOT ONE is stamped edition 1 through 7.

SS 8.65 DATES NOTHING ABOUT ITSELF. Its bullets say what the value means - '0 is pre-release, initial release (0601.0), or test data', '1..255 corresponds to document revisions MISB ST 0601.1 thru MISB ST 0601.255' - and say nothing about when the item that carries it entered the standard.
act_1_the_self_refutation_test.what_this_confirms_rather_than_discovers: reconciliation_ruling already recorded, of the .14-to-.19 delta, that the requirement delta is enumerable from the stamps 'but it does not bound the ITEM delta, and the item delta is the one a tag table would need'. That was written looking FORWARD from .14. This round looked BACKWARD from .14 to .1 and met the same wall from the other side. The item delta is not enumerable in EITHER direction from anything held. Registered as KLV 14.

act_2_the_unconditional_ruling.the_framing_layer_is_correct_as_shipped: Item 22's four octets are introduced by a valid, minimal, short-form BER length. walk_local_set reads the length the stream states, yields four opaque octets, and moves the cursor by four. That is ST 0107.3-04 satisfied the way this codec satisfies it, which is STRUCTURALLY: the walk knows no tags at all, so item 22 is exactly as unknown to it as item 2. A walk that flagged a Required Length would be a walk consulting the tag table, which is the one thing the framing layer is built not to do. NOTHING IS OWED IN klv_codec.
act_2_the_unconditional_ruling.no_fixture_is_written_and_that_is_the_ru: There is no codec defect to reproduce. A synthetic fixture asserting a defect that does not exist would encode this round's confusion as a golden file, which is the round-trip trap this package's README names.
act_2_the_unconditional_ruling.the_flag_is_owed_by_the_value_decoding_l: That layer reads the tag table, and Required Length is a tag-table fact. It does not exist and is blocked on parks 3, 5, 11 and 12.
act_2_the_unconditional_ruling.why_it_is_recorded_unconditioned: Recorded now and unconditioned on the edition question precisely so that neither of Act 1's two possible outcomes reopens it. Whether item 65's 0x01 is trustworthy changes what item 22's four octets MEAN, and changes nothing about which layer owes the check.

the_disposition.outcome: PARKED. Item 22's four octets are parked with the classification undecided, and there are THREE candidates rather than two.
the_disposition.candidate_a: A stream defect against ST 0601.13-29, 'the KLV encoded value for the item shall use exactly the number of bytes specified by the Required Length'. AND NOTE WHAT THE IDENTIFIER ITSELF SAYS: ST 0601.13-29 is stamped EDITION 13, so by the convention above it entered the standard twelve revisions AFTER the edition this stream declares. Under the declared-edition reading the requirement did not exist when this emitter was written. That is not a refutation of (a) - a stream can be defective against the standard as it now stands - but it is exactly why (a) cannot simply be asserted.
the_disposition.candidate_b: Edition skew against ST 0601.1's own item-22 entry, if that edition has one and states a different length.
the_disposition.candidate_c: An unknown tag under the declared edition, if item 22 postdates edition 1. In that case the four octets are simply opaque, a decoder conforming to the declared edition skips them by ST 0107.3-04, and THE LENGTH QUESTION NEVER ARISES.
the_disposition.ruled_out_on_held_bytes: TRANSMISSION CORRUPTION. All six checksums validate over their whole packets, so the four octets are what the emitter wrote. That is the one classification this round could close, and it closed it.
the_disposition.the_deciding_fact: ST 0601.1's TAG TABLE. All three surviving candidates turn on one document and the same page of it.
the_disposition.the_new_park: PARK 13, AND IT IS NOW CLOSED - see park_13_ruling_2026_08_26 and parks.the_ones_that_closed.park_13. THIS FIELD IS KEPT AS THE WALK ROUND WROTE IT, because the route it predicted is worth reading against what happened. It read: 'Reopen route: a public fetch of ST 0601.1 from the NSG Registry, under the pin discipline the ST 0107.3 fetch established - obtain the revision the question names rather than the current one, and pin the copy by SHA-256, byte count and page count with its title page read. A real route and not a wish, because the registry serves superseded editions and park 4 was closed by fetching one that way.' THE ROUTE WAS WRONG IN BOTH ITS PARTICULARS AND RIGHT IN ITS CLAIM. Wrong twice: the NSG Registry did not serve the document - nsgreg.nga.mil answers an automated GET with an F5 JavaScript interstitial and gwg.nga.mil answers 403 - and there is no 'ST 0601.1' to fetch, because edition 1 was published as MISB EG 0601.1 (KLV 15). Right in its claim: it was a real route and not a wish, the document was obtained the same day, and the pin discipline it named was applied in full. What the prediction could not have known is the one thing that made the fetch work - that the publisher's own host is mirrored by the Internet Archive, whose CDX index can be queried for filenames rather than guessed at, which is how a document under /misb/docs/eg/ was found by a round looking under /misb/docs/standards/ for a name that never existed.

act_2_the_three_dating_claims_verified_a.why_this_act_exists: The round was motivated by a search summary, and a summary is not evidence. Each claim was re-checked against the fetched documents' own sentences, and a failure at any one would have reopened the corresponding candidate rather than let the round proceed. act_2_the_three_dating_claims_verified_a.i_items_40_through_72_CONFIRMED: EG 0601.1 SS 3, the EG0601.1 row, verbatim: 'Added metadata items 40 through 72 with registered UDS keys, and ESD digraphs as appropriate.' Item 65 lies inside that range, and edition 1 carries it in both places a tag has to appear: the SS 6.1 tag table row reads '65 | UAS LDS Version Number | ... | Number | uint8 | 1', and SS 7.65 'Key 65: UAS LDS Version Number Conversion' defines its value. SO THE STAMP IS DATED AND NOT MERELY UNREFUTED, which is the upgrade this act was for: the walk round could only say that nothing dated item 65's introduction, and edition 1 says item 65 was introduced AT edition 1. A stream stamping item 65 = 0x01 is now self-consistent on held bytes.
act_2_the_three_dating_claims_verified_a.i_addendum_the_stamp_was_OPTIONAL_at_the: NOT ASKED FOR AND FOUND ANYWAY, and it sharpens the stamp rather than weakening it. EG 0601.1 SS 7.65.1 reads: 'This item is not required in every packet of metadata, but is useful when included periodically.' By ST 0601.8-12 - 'All instances of the UAS Datalink LS shall contain Tag 65, UAS LS Version Number' - it is mandatory in every packet, and ST 0601.8 is now held (edition_history) so that requirement is first-hand rather than quoted from st_0601_14. The consequence for the walk round's six packets: an emitter at edition 1 that sends item 65 in every packet is doing MORE than edition 1 asks, which is consistent with the declared-edition reading and is not evidence against it.
act_2_the_three_dating_claims_verified_a.ii_tag_22_in_the_initial_release_CONFIRM: CONFIRMED, and by a DIRECT READ rather than by inference from (i). The inference was available - items 40 through 72 arrived at edition 1, so item 22 predates it - but the initial release itself was obtained, so the claim rests on its table instead. EG 0601 (initial release, 12 Jan 2006), tag table page 14: '22 | Target Width | TBD | Tw | Target Width | ... | Meters | uint16 | 2'. SO CANDIDATE (c) IS DEAD - see act_3_the_ruling.candidate_c_dead. Two internal consistencies fell out of holding it and are recorded because they check the copy rather than the claim: the initial release has NO SS 3 at all, which is what EG 0601.1's 'Added section 3 for modifications and changes' says of it; and its item 22 row carries 'TBD' where EG 0601.1's carries a UDS key, which is what 'Created UDS keys for the existing LDS metadata items which did not previously have a UDS metadata item to map to' says of it.
act_2_the_three_dating_claims_verified_a.iii_the_EG_to_standard_conversion_CONFIR: CONFIRMED verbatim, and it had to come from ST 0601.4 because edition 1 predates the conversion and ST 0601.8's revision history is a single row. ST 0601.4 SS 3, the row 'STD 0601.2 - UAS Datalink Local Data Set.  October 29, 2008': 'Change the status from Engineering Guideline to Standard in order to enforce requirements upon developers implementing this document.' and, the next line, 'Wording changed to make requirements enforceable.' SO EDITION 1 IS NON-NORMATIVE BY THE SERIES' OWN ACCOUNT, and that is the qualifier act_3_the_ruling carries rather than a hedge added to it.

act_3_the_ruling.the_row_read_from_the_held_edition: EG 0601.1's tag table, SS 6.1, page 15. Its own column list is 'KEY | LDS Name | Mapped UDS | ESD | ESD Name | UDS | UDS Name | Units | Format | Len | Notes', and the item 22 row reads: KEY '22', LDS Name 'Target Width', Units 'Meters', Format 'uint16', LEN '2', Notes 'Target Width within sensor field of view. Map 0..(2^16-1) to 0..10000 meters. 1 meter = 3.2808399 feet. Resolution: ~.16 meters.'
act_3_the_ruling.the_length_is_stated_THREE_TIMES_INSIDE_: The disjunction sweep run on the one value the whole park turned on, and all three agree. (1) The tag table's Len column: 2. (2) SS 7.22's header block: 'LDS Key 22 | Units Range Format | ... | Meters | 0..10,000 | uint16'. (3) SS 7.22's WORKED EXAMPLE, which is the strongest of the three because it is the document encoding the item itself rather than describing it: '1234.56789 Meters [K][L][V] = [0d22][0d2][0x1F 9B]' - a length octet of 0d2 and two value octets.
act_3_the_ruling.candidate_c_dead: DEAD, on the ground the disposition table itself set: (c) required that 'ST 0601.1's tag table has no item 22 at all'. Edition 1 has item 22, and so does the initial release before it. The four octets are therefore NOT an unknown tag under the declared edition, the ST 0107.3-04 skip is not the applicable reading, and the length question does arise.
act_3_the_ruling.candidate_b_dead: DEAD, and this is the candidate the round expected to win. (b) required 'that ST 0601.1 defines item 22 with a Required Length of 4, or with none'. It defines it with a Len of 2 - the same as st_0601_14's SS 8.22 - so there is no edition skew to find. The item's length did not change at any point this repository can sample: uint16 and 2 at the initial release (12 January 2006), at edition 1, at .4, at .8, at .14a and at .19, which is six sample points spanning 12 January 2006 to 11 June 2025.
act_3_the_ruling.the_ruling_is_a: (a), A STREAM DEFECT. The six packets' four octets under item 22 diverge from the length the standard states, and - this is what the fetch changed - they diverge from the length THE EMITTER'S OWN DECLARED EDITION states. The disposition table's objection to (a) is answered from a direction the table did not anticipate. That objection was that ST 0601.13-29 is stamped edition 13, twelve revisions after the declared edition, so under the declared-edition reading the requirement did not exist when the emitter was written. It is answered not by dismissing the stamp but by reading edition 1: the LENGTH never changed, so both readings of the stamp now reach the same classification. There is no edition of this series in which four octets was correct, and the emitter is not sheltered by its own stamp under any reading. THAT CONVERGENCE IS WHAT CLOSES THE PARK: (a) was unassertable before because the two readings disagreed, and they no longer do.
act_3_the_ruling.the_qualifier_act_2_iii_supplies_and_it_: AT EDITION 1 THE DIVERGENCE IS FROM A GUIDELINE. The document is an Engineering Guideline and ST 0601.4 SS 3 says the .2 conversion was made 'in order to enforce requirements upon developers implementing this document' with 'Wording changed to make requirements enforceable' - so by the series' own account edition 1 stated lengths as direction and not as enforceable requirements. The defect's two bases are therefore different and are kept apart: its FACTUAL basis is edition 1's own table and every edition after it, and its NORMATIVE basis is ST 0601.13-29, which is the current standard's. Saying only the first would overstate what an EG can require; saying only the second would leave the objection the disposition table raised unanswered.
act_3_the_ruling.what_the_ruling_does_NOT_say: It does not say the stream is worthless, and it does not say the emitter is non-conformant at the edition it declares in any sense edition 1 could enforce. It says the four octets are a defect against the standard as it stands and a divergence from every edition including the declared one. It also does not touch the checksums: all six still validate, so the four octets are what the emitter wrote, which walk_ruling_real_stream_2026_08_26 established and this round did not revisit.

edition_history.what_this_is: THE 0601 LINEAGE, NOT PINS. The governing text remains ST 0601.14 alone, edition 1 is pinned separately at delegated_specifications_held.eg_0601_1 as park 13's deciding document, and no row in FORMAT_COVERAGE.md is read against any of these three files. They exist so that a claim about when something was introduced can be checked against the standard's own change records rather than recalled - which is verbatim the reason cat048's edition_history states, and this lineage was built on that precedent deliberately rather than inventing a third shape.
edition_history.editions_in_hand: EG 0601 (initial release, 12 Jan 2006), STD 0601.4 (4 March 2010) and MISB ST 0601.8 (23 October 2014).
edition_history.what_each_one_is_here_for: EACH CARRIES SOMETHING THE OTHERS DO NOT, which is the test for whether a lineage file earns its place. ST 0601.4: carries the full SS 3 revision history back to the initial release, which no later edition does, and with it the sentence that makes edition 1 non-normative ('Change the status from Engineering Guideline to Standard in order to enforce requirements upon developers implementing this document'). AMENDED 2026-08-27: 'these are obtainable' was true when written and is now false in practice. The parks round tried all three routes and every one refused - gwg.nga.mil answered nothing at all, nsgreg.nga.mil answered nothing, and web.archive.org answered HTTP 429 with X-RL: 0 on the CDX API and on playback alike, INCLUDING on the byte-exact archived URL recorded above as having served ST0601.4.pdf. So the throttle is the archive's own rate limiting and is not specific to these documents. No credentials and no account are involved: it is a quota, and the route is expected to work again. Recorded because a record field asserting obtainability is exactly the kind of claim that rots without anybody editing it. RETRIED ONCE, 2026-08-27T14:05Z, and the route is still throttled: the CDX API and playback both answered HTTP 429 with Server: nginx and X-RL: 1, a 162-byte error page, on the byte-exact archived ST0601.4.pdf URL recorded above as well as on a fresh index query. X-RL was 0 at the previous observation and 1 at this one, so the counter moved and the refusal did not; two samples say nothing more than that. THE SAME RETRY WITHDRAWS PART OF THIS FIELD'S OWN AMENDMENT. It says gwg.nga.mil and nsgreg.nga.mil each answered nothing at all, which reads as two hosts declining an automated GET. What is reproducible is that the entire nga.mil zone does not resolve from this environment - SERVFAIL for gwg.nga.mil, nsgreg.nga.mil, www.nga.mil and the nga.mil apex, from the only resolver reachable here, which answers normally for web.archive.org and www.nist.gov - and that no independent resolver can be reached to cross-check, since outbound port 53 to 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 times out on every query. So no request was sent to either host and neither of them refused anything: the failure was a name that did not resolve, which is a fact about this environment and not about the MISB's hosts. It is finding 4's class one layer down, a probe reporting a property of itself as a property of its target, and the correction makes the blocker SMALLER - one throttled route rather than three refusing hosts. The prose record of the retry, with the response headers in full, is at FORMAT_COVERAGE.md's park 9 section. RETRIED A SECOND TIME, 2026-08-27T14:51Z, and every recorded term is unchanged: the CDX index query and playback of the byte-exact archived ST0601.4.pdf URL above both answered HTTP 429 with Server: nginx, X-RL: 1, Content-Type: text/html and a 162-byte body, which was read and NOT hashed. NO BYTES ARRIVED, so this pin's sha256 was neither contradicted nor confirmed by the retry - the digest comparison the park's plan puts before any reading was never reached, and the round claims nothing about the copy. X-RL has now been sampled three times, 0 then 1 then 1; the counter moves and the refusal does not, and three samples say no more than two did, so it is recorded as a non-finding rather than as a trend. THE ENVIRONMENT BOUND WAS RE-DERIVED BEFORE THE NETWORK WAS TRUSTED, which is the order the previous retry's own correction argues for: the nga.mil zone still answers SERVFAIL at gwg.nga.mil, nsgreg.nga.mil and the apex from the only reachable resolver, while web.archive.org resolves normally in the same run. So exactly one of the three routes could be asked, the same one as before, and the two official routes remain a question this environment cannot put. No mirror was improvised. day_flight_provenance_2026_08_26.what_this_is: THE PROVENANCE ROUND. It was sent after ONE unverified lead against a closed park - that the held stream might be one of the 'supplementary test files' EG 0601.1 SS 3 says replaced its Appendix A - and the lead DID NOT VERIFY. It is closed as UNVERIFIABLE FROM THE ROUTES THIS REPOSITORY CAN REACH, with every route and its failure mode enumerated so nobody re-runs the hunt. What verified instead is the question nobody had asked: WHERE THE HELD BYTES CAME FROM. The answer is samples.ffmpeg.org, established by byte identity, and it is not MISB. Stated in that order because a round that verifies an adjacent fact and reports itself as a round that verified the lead is the failure this file exists to prevent. See FORMAT_COVERAGE.md's section 'The Day Flight provenance round'. THIS ROUND FETCHED NO SPECIFICATION AND PINNED NONE: the ten documents in fixtures/klv/spec/ are unchanged and seven of them are still pins.

the_verification_standard_and_why_it_was.the_standard: BYTE IDENTITY AGAINST A COPY MISB SERVED. The lead upgraded to verified only on a sha256 match to a491ceff524b0008e3076d9eb30782badac2d53053731accc0a4e1226177260e from a MISB-served file. A same-named file with DIFFERENT bytes would have been a distinct finding - it would show MISB published a Day Flight and not this one - and a listing naming the file without serving bytes would have been corroboration recorded BELOW verification.
the_verification_standard_and_why_it_was.what_was_produced: NONE OF THE THREE. No MISB-served bytes, no same-named file with different bytes, no MISB listing naming the file in text.
the_verification_standard_and_why_it_was.what_this_is_not: IT IS NOT A REFUTATION. MISB's own test-file area was account-gated and is not in the index (see the_corroboration), so absence there is not evidence of absence. The lead is unverified and unverifiable from held routes, which is a weaker and more accurate statement than refuted.

act_1_the_routes_each_with_its_failure_m.route_1_wayback_cdx_of_the_MISB_host: THE ROUTE THAT PRODUCED EG 0601.1, so it was taken first and it is proven. Two queries. The prefix query url=gwg.nga.mil/misb* returned 720 rows; the host query returned 2961 unique URLs of which 770 are under /misb. DERIVED FROM THE DUMPS, NOT TYPED: video/* MIME types under /misb/ = 0; URLs on the whole host matching 'flight' or 'night' = 0; URLs ending .mpg, .mpeg or .m2t = 0. The single video/* anywhere on the host is a .wmv animation under /ntb/. The /misb/ subtree has exactly five content areas - docs/ (336), data/ (138), images/ (56), style/ (17), scripts/ (8) - and no test-file area among them. FAILURE MODE: the public MISB site never served motion imagery at all, and this is NOT 'the crawler missed it' - MISB says so itself, see the_corroboration.
act_1_the_routes_each_with_its_failure_m.route_1b_the_sites_own_machine_readable_: The pages under /misb/ render from /misb/data/*.xml, so the catalogue is where a published test file would be NAMED even if the bytes were elsewhere. zip_pubs.xml lists five entries and every one is a '...CompositeDocuments.zip' - DOCUMENT bundles. eg_pubs.xml and trm_pubs.xml name no media of any kind. AND THE ONE ARCHIVE THE PUBLIC HOST EVER SERVED IS CLOSED BY ARITHMETIC: AllMISBDocs.zip is 20081234 bytes, smaller than the 102004664-byte stream, so it cannot contain it. FAILURE MODE: the catalogue that would have named a test file names none.
act_1_the_routes_each_with_its_failure_m.route_1c_the_live_host_rechecked_rather_: https://gwg.nga.mil/misb/ and https://gwg.nga.mil/misb/docs/standards/ST0601.19.pdf, each with a browser User-Agent and a same-origin Referer: 403 BOTH. The refusal delegated_specifications_held.eg_0601_1.source_is_a_MIRROR_and_not_the_registry records still holds, checked this round rather than carried forward on trust.
act_1_the_routes_each_with_its_failure_m.route_2_MISB_adjacent_hosts: THE HOST SET IS DERIVED AND NOT GUESSED: the hosts the archived MISB pages themselves link out to - www.nga.mil, jitc.fhu.disa.mil and aafassociation.org - plus nsgreg.nga.mil, the registry this record already names. Unique URLs in the CDX index: nsgreg.nga.mil 17806, www.nga.mil 26837, jitc.fhu.disa.mil 14310, aafassociation.org 1442. Motion-imagery test streams on any of them: NONE. www.nga.mil holds the only .mpg files in the whole sweep - five, and all five are under /ngakids/ or /kids/, children's educational clips. With gwg.nga.mil's 2961 that is 63356 unique URLs across five hosts. FAILURE MODE: no MISB-adjacent host in the index hosts sample streams, and the one MISB's own pages say does is the account-gated protected site.
act_1_the_routes_each_with_its_failure_m.route_3_the_sample_collections_own_prove: THE ROUTE THAT ANSWERED A DIFFERENT QUESTION. No README exists in MPEG2/mpegts-klv/, in MPEG2/, or at the server root: README and README.txt both 404. The root 00-README is 728 bytes and describes the collection ('This is the MPlayer samples collection'), stating nothing per file. THE COLLECTION'S OWN CONVENTION for recording what a sample is, is a sibling .txt: 2308 of the 16949 entries in allsamples.txt carry one, and NEITHER 'Day Flight.mpg' NOR 'Night Flight IR.mpg' does. allsamples.txt matches 'misb' or 'nga.mil' 0 times. FAILURE MODE: the server states no origin for this file, and the one convention it has for saying where a sample came from was not used here - so route 3 ends in an ABSENCE THAT WAS CHECKED rather than one assumed.
act_1_the_routes_each_with_its_failure_m.what_route_3_did_establish: The origin of the HELD COPY, by byte identity, recorded on the pin itself at walk_ruling_real_stream_2026_08_26.the_two_pins.transport_stream.origin_url and its two neighbouring fields. The directory also holds one sibling, 'Night Flight IR.mpg' at 162M, and a PAIR is exactly what a published SET of test files looks like - which is why the lead was worth running routes against rather than dismissing. The pair is not evidence of a publisher.
act_1_the_routes_each_with_its_failure_m.the_bytes_have_not_moved_since_at_least_: The earliest Wayback capture of the directory listing (20140116012639) prints 'Day Flight.mpg 06-Oct-2012 02:38 97M'; the live listing prints '2012-10-06 03:38 97M'. The hour differs because Apache renders a listing in server-local time and the offset changed; the last-modified header is the fact and it is the same instant. Both listings are held.

the_corroboration_recorded_BELOW_verific.what_it_is: MISB'S OWN WEBSITE SAYS ITS TEST FILES WERE BEHIND A LOGIN, and that is what converts route 1's zero from a gap into an explanation. The archived FAQ, capture 20091221094307, under the question 'Where is the MISB website, and what can I find there?', says the public site holds the MISP and the current Standards, RPs and EGs, and then, verbatim: 'If you need access to draft documents, test files, and other support documentation follow the instructions on the website to apply for an account to access the MISB protected website.'
the_corroboration_recorded_BELOW_verific.the_protected_site_is_not_reachable_eith: Of the 21 /protected/ captures in the gwg.nga.mil host dump, 17 report HTTP 401, 3 are redirects and 1 is a 404 - including the MISB protected index itself, https://www.gwg.nga.mil/protected/misb/index.html, captured 20130215184001 as 401. THE ARCHIVE HOLDS THE REFUSAL AND NOT THE CONTENT.
the_corroboration_recorded_BELOW_verific.the_changelog_sentence_is_corroborated_a: The standing rule is that a fetch contradicting the changelog sentence that motivated the lead stops the round. Nothing contradicts it. EG 0601.1 SS 3 says supplementary test files were to be provided on the MISB website; the FAQ, written a year or two later, says test files were on the MISB website behind an account. THOSE AGREE. What no held byte says is that any of them was named 'Day Flight', and that is exactly the join the lead needed and did not get.
the_corroboration_recorded_BELOW_verific.why_this_is_corroboration_and_not_verifi: It corroborates the CHANGELOG SENTENCE - that MISB had test files - and not the LEAD, which is that this file is one of them. The FAQ names no filename. Filed below verification on the briefing's own standard.

act_3_the_consequence_for_PARK_13_is_NON.the_classification_is_unaffected_either_: AND IT WOULD HAVE BEEN UNAFFECTED HAD THE LEAD VERIFIED, which is the sharper claim and the one worth stating. The ruling's two bases are a FACTUAL one - EG 0601.1's own tag table states a Len of 2 at three sites inside itself and every edition after it agrees - and a NORMATIVE one, ST 0601.13-29. THE PUBLISHER OF THE FILE IS AN INPUT TO NEITHER. Four octets against a stated length of two is four octets against a stated length of two whether MISB served the clip, FFmpeg's sample collection served it, or a sensor wrote it in a hangar. park_13_ruling_2026_08_26.the_day_flight_test_file_lead_UNVERIFIED already said as much; this round TESTED that sentence instead of relying on it.
act_3_the_consequence_for_PARK_13_is_NON.KLV_15_and_KLV_16_do_not_move_either: Both are findings about edition 1's IDENTITY - the name ST 0601.14a SS 8.65 sends readers to that was never published, and the date edition 1 states three ways - and neither takes evidence from a stream. THE REGISTER DID NOT GROW: it holds 16 entries and gains no seventeenth. The origin gap this round closed is a defect in THIS REPOSITORY'S pinning and not an ambiguity in a specification, and the register's subject is the documents.
act_3_the_consequence_for_PARK_13_is_NON.what_the_failure_to_verify_DOES_cost: THE ONE THING THE LEAD WAS RAISED TO BUY. It existed because a defect in a FIELDED EMITTER and a defect in a PUBLISHED TEST FILE are different findings about the same octets, and the origin now known cannot separate them: a third-party sample collection with no provenance note says nothing about which of the two produced these six packets. So that question is not closed - it is closed TO THIS ROUND'S ROUTES.
act_3_the_consequence_for_PARK_13_is_NON.the_reopen_condition: EXACT AND NARROW: a copy of a MISB-published test file whose sha256 is a491ceff524b0008e3076d9eb30782badac2d53053731accc0a4e1226177260e, or a MISB listing that names 'Day Flight' in text. The account-gated protected site is where either would be, and this repository cannot reach it. APPLYING FOR AN NGA ACCOUNT IS NOT A FETCH - it is a relationship, and it is outside what a round like this can do.

the_briefing_correction_the_adjudication.what_is_corrected: THE SECOND BRIEFING DEFECT THIS SECTION HAS RECORDED, and unlike the first it is a DEFINITION rather than a premise. The adjudication round's briefing defined candidate (a) in a way that required ST 0601.13-29 to be normative AT THE EDITION THE STREAM DECLARES - and its own Act 2(iii) refuted that: ST 0601.4 SS 3 states the .2 conversion was made 'in order to enforce requirements upon developers implementing this document' with 'Wording changed to make requirements enforceable', so edition 1 is an Engineering Guideline stating lengths as direction and not as enforceable requirements. An EG does not carry the normativity that definition demanded, so a candidate defined that way could never have been assertable and the round would have had to park on its own terms.
the_briefing_correction_the_adjudication.what_supersedes_it: THE RULING'S FACTUAL/NORMATIVE SPLIT, at park_13_ruling_2026_08_26.act_3_the_ruling.the_qualifier_act_2_iii_supplies_and_it_is_not_a_hedge. (a) rests on edition 1's own table for WHAT THE LENGTH IS and on ST 0601.13-29 for WHAT A DIVERGENCE FROM IT MEANS TODAY - two bases, two documents, kept apart precisely so neither has to do the other's work. That split is load-bearing and the briefing's single-basis definition is withdrawn.
the_briefing_correction_the_adjudication.filed_alongside_the_withdrawn_era_premis: walk_ruling_real_stream_2026_08_26.the_briefing_defect_withdrawn holds the first defect - the 'ST 0601.8-era' claim from the droneklv README, a decoder's supported edition read as an emitter's. This one is filed beside it on the same rule, which is settlement 3's corrected epoch premise: a definition that turned out incoherent is EVIDENCE about how this section reaches conclusions, and deleting it keeps the habit while removing the evidence.
the_briefing_correction_the_adjudication.the_standing_annotation_that_is_CARRIED_: ST 0601.13-29'S RETROACTIVITY IS STILL UNESTABLISHED. The identifier is stamped edition 13, nothing held says a requirement introduced at 13 reaches an emitter written against edition 1, and park 13 closing did not establish it - the park closed because edition 1's own table supplies the FACTUAL basis, which is a different move from establishing retroactivity. So this is candidate (a)'s STANDING ANNOTATION and not a loose end that closure tidied away. See also walk_ruling_real_stream_2026_08_26 candidate_a, which raised the objection first.

witnessed_set_ruling_2026_08_26.what_this_is: THE WITNESSED-SET COVERAGE ROUND OF 2026-08-26, and the round that shipped adapter #10. The four rounds before it each ended in a park: the framing round established the key and the tag, the length round closed park 4 and got the length grammar, the walk round found six packets and decoded no value, and the adjudication and provenance rounds ruled item 22 a stream defect and pinned the stream's origin. act_1_the_enumeration.method: klv_uas_codec.decode_stream over the 977 octets. Every count below is that function's output and NONE was carried from the walk round's record - which is the point of re-deriving them: they agree item for item, and an agreement between two independent derivations is worth more than a quotation of one.
act_1_the_enumeration.length_divergences: 1 - item 22, at all six sites, four octets against a Required Length of 2. Park 13 already ruled it a stream defect. 155 of the 156 items carry exactly the octet count their own SS 8.x block requires.

the_transcription_and_the_checks_that_an.source: MISB ST 0601.14a, SHA-256 3d5f1ca105befe6f48023a3cdd29262883d6b77c73c06ba915c4da91ab212ce4, fixtures/klv/spec/ST0601.14a.pdf - each item's own SS 8.x block, read cell by drawn cell against column boundaries taken from that block's own header row, which is the discipline tag_table_st_0601_14.how_it_was_transcribed sets out for Table 1
the_transcription_and_the_checks_that_an.the_map_is_one_affine_form_stated_twice_: software = (software_max - software_min) / (klv_max - klv_min) * klv_integer + offset. The document states it as two formulas and again as a 'Map A..B to C..D' bullet, so the transcription is checkable against the block's own second statement of it.
the_transcription_and_the_checks_that_an.check_1_the_pinned_editions_own_examples: 26 of 26 agree. Every SS 8.x block prints one Software Value beside the KLV octets that encode it, and SS 7's Programmer's Notes say why: 'the "Example Value" for a tag is shown in full precision, beyond a tag's resolution, so programmers can verify they are using the right formulas.' Run by klv_uas_codec.check_against_the_documents_own_examples() on every suite run.
the_transcription_and_the_checks_that_an.check_2_edition_1s_own_examples: 23 of 23 decode, each within one quantisation step of the value EG 0601.1's own SS 7.N prints. A SECOND, INDEPENDENT set of octets over the same 26 maps, answering a different question: not 'is the transcription right' but 'did the map move between edition 1 and the pinned one'. Items 40, 41 and 42 have a SS 7.N section and no worked example, which is why 23 and not 26, and the checker reports the absence rather than skipping it silently.
the_transcription_and_the_checks_that_an.what_the_two_checks_together_establish: The ranges and formats of all 26 witnessed items are identical in EG 0601.1 (15 May 2008) and ST 0601.14a (1 May 2020). Twelve years, thirteen revisions, sampled at both ends, and the only column that moved is the Format name on the two string items - register entry KLV 17. That is the item-22 finding generalised from one Len cell to the whole witnessed set.

act_2_the_length_divergence_policy.why_it_was_owed_here: Park 13 decided what item 22's four octets MEAN and said explicitly what it did not reach: the framing layer is 'correct as shipped' and 'the flag is owed by the value-decoding layer, which does not exist'. That layer is adapters/klv_uas_codec.py and it exists now.
act_2_the_length_divergence_policy.candidate_a_reject_the_packet_REJECTED: All six checksums validate, so the packet is exactly what the emitter wrote and 25 of its 26 items carry conformant lengths; discarding them on account of one item destroys verified data. It also contradicts ST 0107.3-04, whose entire subject is that one item must not take the others down. A length a decoder cannot use makes the ITEM unusable, not the packet.
act_2_the_length_divergence_policy.candidate_c_decode_anyway_REJECTED: Reaching 457 from 0x000001c9 requires CHOOSING a rule - strip leading octets to the Required Length, read the whole field as the wider unsigned integer, or take the low Required-Length octets - and no held document states any of them. The three agree on THIS stream and disagree the moment a top octet is non-zero, so their agreeing here is a property of the stream rather than of the rule.
act_2_the_length_divergence_policy.factual_basis: edition 1's own item table states this item's Len at three sites inside itself, and every edition this repository can sample states the same one — the initial release (12 January 2006), EG 0601.1, STD 0601.4, ST 0601.8, ST 0601.14a and ST 0601.19. See FORMAT_COVERAGE.md, 'Park 13 adjudicated and CLOSED', for the reading, and MISB EG 0601.1, SHA-256 1714322c25e00e00ccabd5d861318f1448055cbf2000dc2e5099fb30dec0b730, fixtures/klv/spec/EG0601.1.pdf for the copy
act_2_the_length_divergence_policy.normative_basis: ST 0601.13-29, §7: 'When a metadata item has a Required Length numerically specified in this standard, the KLV encoded value for the item shall use exactly the number of bytes specified by the Required Length.' STANDING ANNOTATION, carried rather than shed at closure: the identifier is stamped edition 13, nothing held establishes that a requirement introduced at edition 13 reaches an emitter written against an earlier edition, and that retroactivity is still unestablished. It is why this basis is stated BESIDE the factual one and never instead of it

class_boundaries_the_document_draws.required_length_divergence: DEFECT. ST 0601.13-29, SS 7: 'When a metadata item has a Required Length numerically specified in this standard, the KLV encoded value for the item shall use exactly the number of bytes specified by the Required Length.'
class_boundaries_the_document_draws.variable_length_item_under_its_max: NOT IN THE CLASS. Required Length is N/A, so there is nothing to diverge from. The pinned stream's item 11 varies between 2 and 3 octets.
class_boundaries_the_document_draws.variable_length_item_over_its_max: §7 defines Max Length as 'the recommended maximum length' and names its consumer — 'Network guards may use this value as a check to prevent data leaks' — so exceeding it breaks no 'shall' and the item is decoded. Recorded as an advisory rather than skipped, because applying ST 0601.13-29's requirement to a recommendation would enforce a rule the document did not write
class_boundaries_the_document_draws.zero_length_item: ST 0601.14-33, §6.5: 'Where a UAS Data-link LS item has a length of zero, consumers shall interpret the value of the item as "unknown".' §6.5 states the mechanism: 'the producer sends a Zero-Length Item (ZLI) which is a Local Set item with no value (i.e. tag followed by a length of zero, with no value). The receiver interprets a ZLI as the value becoming immediately Unknown.' So this is an explicit unknown and not a defect, and never a zero
class_boundaries_the_document_draws.zero_length_item_on_tag_1_2_or_65: ST 0601.14-32, §6.5: 'Required items of a UAS Datalink LS (Tag 1 - Checksum, Tag 2 - Precision Time Stamp, and Tag 65 - UAS Datalink LS Version Number) instance shall always be reported with positive lengths (i.e. Zero-Length Items (ZLI) are not allowed for these items).' A ZLI on one of those three is the one zero-length case the document itself makes a defect
class_boundaries_the_document_draws.st_0601_14_34_not_enforced: 'A Zero-Length Item (ZLI) shall only be used in packets after a non-ZLI is reported' is a constraint on a PRODUCER ACROSS PACKETS. Checking it would carry state from one packet into the next, which is the accumulation this section refuses in every settlement it has written. The ZLI is recorded per packet and a consumer holding the sequence can apply the rule.

act_2_the_length_divergence_policy.tested_with: Five synthetic fixtures, one per row of the table above, reproducing the CLASS and not the stream: length_divergence_at_a_required_length carries 0x00000FA0 where the stream carries 0x000001c9, because a golden file built from a real emitter's defective octets would make this repository's suite a place where somebody else's stream lives.

observations_filed_and_not_acted_on.target_location_equals_frame_centre: Items 40/41/42 are BYTE-IDENTICAL to 23/24/25 at all six sites. The emitter is answering SS 8.40's own conditional - 'This is the crosshair location if different from frame center' - with 'not different'. The adapter carries both and reconciles neither, which is precisely the case where a merge would look free.
observations_filed_and_not_acted_on.frame_centre_elevation_against_the_impli: Item 25 decodes to about -4.5 m MSL at 54.75N 110.05W; the sensor is at about 1532 m MSL with a relative elevation of about -4.4 degrees and a slant range of about 10.9 km, which puts the frame centre near 690 m. A ~700 m disagreement.
