publisher_round_2026_09_03.the_finding_worth_carrying_out: A GUARD CAN ONLY CHECK THE TIER ITS SUBJECT LIVES ON, AND THE LABEL DOES NOT DECIDE THAT. The park 8 guard in tests/test_cdm_format_coverage.py was written as a suite check and its subject - whether a publisher sells a document - lived at pub.smpte.org, which no test here can reach. It was green for eleven days over a claim that was false the whole time, and it was green BECAUSE it was doing its job: it required the record to keep saying the thing, and the record kept saying it. The guard now reads the closure, whose evidence is two PDFs on disk with digests, page counts and title-page identities - things the suite CAN reach. THAT IS AN IMPROVEMENT IN TIER AND NOT IN KIND: it is still the tree agreeing with itself, and the difference is that the tree now contains the bytes the claim is about. The general form: before writing a guard, ask where its subject lives. If the answer is a host, a registry or a price, the guard can pin the record's WORDING and cannot pin the FACT, and saying so at the guard is the only honest arrangement. Rule 12 already covers the reading; this covers the check built on top of one.
publisher_round_2026_09_03.the_rounds_own_history_and_it_is_not_a_w: THE BRIEF'S FIRST ISSUE STOPPED AT ACT 0 ON TWO OF ITS OWN BOOKKEEPING FIGURES. It asserted a clean working tree while an untracked input directory sat in the working root, and it asserted a sweep of 8 files and 18 lines where the three-pattern sweep it specified returns 9 and 27 - the 8/18 pair being the counts for a single-pattern grep. It was corrected and re-issued with the tree untouched between the runs, and the second issue's Act 0 was re-taken from scratch rather than carried. THE FIRST ISSUE'S FIGURES WERE STILL WRONG ON RE-ISSUE AT ONE POINT: the input directory had not in fact been moved, and Act 0.1 read 1 rather than 0 again. It was moved out of the working root before Act 1 and 0.1 was re-taken at 0. Recorded because a round that stops on a premise and then proceeds on the same premise's second statement should say so; this is the round's history and not an exemption from anything.

text_pin_ruling.what_this_is: THE TEXT-PINS ROUND OF 2026-09-04, AND IT IS THE SCHEMA RULING THE SURFACE ROUND STOPPED FOR. That round went to acquire IETF RFC 2781, found it free, stable, erratum-free and served over a route that answered 200 on the first ask, and could not pin it: the RFC Editor issues no PDF for it and every gate here recognised a pin by `.pdf`. It named four sites and said 'any one of those is a ruling; four of them together are a round'. This node is that round's two rulings, and the acquisition it unblocked was one GET.
text_pin_ruling.ruling_1_a_pin_may_be_text_where_the_pub: RULED BY M ON 2026-09-04. **A PIN MAY BE TEXT WHERE THE PUBLISHER ISSUES NO PDF.** The copy that is read is the publisher's `.txt` AS SERVED — not a conversion, not a rendering, not the HTML sibling reduced to text. WHAT IS BEING RULED IS NARROW AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT: this is not a licence to pin any text file, and it is not a preference for text. It is the recognition that a pin's job — let a reader holding a copy establish that they hold the same document — is done by a digest, a byte count and the document's own arithmetic about itself, and that NONE OF THOSE THREE IS A PROPERTY OF PDF. The PDF-shaped gates were reading a container where they meant an identity, and the container was load-bearing only by accident of every publisher this repository had met so far issuing one.

the_fields_a_text_pin_carries.field_sha256: THE SAME FIELD, computed from the copy at `local_path` rather than taken as given, exactly as every PDF pin's is. This is the term that does the identity work and it is format-blind.
the_fields_a_text_pin_carries.field_bytes: THE SAME FIELD, computed from the local copy.
the_fields_a_text_pin_carries.field_pages: KEPT, and produced by the SECOND ruled method — see `page_count_method.the_paginated_text_variant_ruled_2026_09_04`. Form feeds counted, `[Page N]` footers counted, and the highest footer number: all three must agree. A text document with no pagination of its own carries no `pages` field at all rather than a zero.
the_fields_a_text_pin_carries.field_lines: NEW, AND DEFINED RATHER THAN LEFT TO A LIBRARY: **the count of `\n` bytes**, which is `wc -l` semantics. RFC 2781 gives 787. THE DEFINITION IS THE FIELD, and the reason is in the next node.
the_fields_a_text_pin_carries.field_format: NEW. `"text/plain"` for a text pin. **A NODE WITHOUT THE FIELD IS A PDF**, which is the arrangement that keeps twelve existing nodes untouched by this ruling: a round that had to add `"format": "application/pdf"` to twelve records to admit a thirteenth would be rewriting twelve pins to describe one, and every one of those rewrites is a diff a reader has to check against bytes that did not move. The default is stated here, once, and the gates read it here.
the_fields_a_text_pin_carries.field_local_path: THE SAME FIELD. `gates/pin_paths.py` needed NO widening to resolve it — its `discover()` carries no extension filter by deliberate design and its `<kind>` segment selects the base — so the path resolution this ruling might have been expected to break was already format-blind. Recorded because it is the one gate the surface round named that turned out to need nothing.
the_fields_a_text_pin_carries.WHY_THESE_KEYS_ARE_PREFIXED_AND_IT_IS_A_: THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS NODE NAMED ITS KEYS `sha256`, `bytes`, `pages`, `lines`, `format` and `local_path` — the fields themselves, which reads well and is wrong. `gates/pin_paths.py`'s `discover()` walks EVERY dict in EVERY pin record and treats any node carrying both a `local_path` string and a `sha256` string as a pin, by deliberate design: it has no extension filter, because choosing the base per pin is its whole job. So a node DESCRIBING the fields was discovered AS a pin, and the gate crashed trying to read `int("THE SAME FIELD, computed from the local copy.")`. **IT CRASHED RATHER THAN PASSING, AND THAT IS THE ONLY REASON THIS IS A FOOTNOTE AND NOT AN INCIDENT.** Had the prose happened to be a numeral the gate would have reported a fourteenth pin with a 64-character digest it could not resolve, which is a wrong count reported cleanly — the failure mode this whole record is organised against. The keys are prefixed `field_` so the description of a schema cannot be mistaken for an instance of it, and the lesson generalises past this node: in a record that is walked structurally, a key is an interface and not a label.

text_pin_ruling.the_lines_definition_and_the_787_versus_: **787 BY THE RULED METHOD, 801 BY `str.splitlines()`, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS EXACTLY THE PAGE COUNT.** Python's `str.splitlines()` treats the form feed 0x0C as a line terminator; `wc -l` and `str.count('\n')` do not. RFC 2781 carries 14 form feeds, so the two figures differ by 14 — 801 - 787 = 14 — and a `lines` value taken one way and checked the other differs by the page count WITH NO ERROR ANYWHERE. That is the same defect shape `gates/pdf_text.py` exists for and the same shape `page_count_method`'s own correction records: two methods that agree on the ordinary case, disagree on this one, and neither announces itself. THE RULED FIGURE IS 787, the `\n` count, chosen because it is what `wc -l` reports and `wc -l` is what a reader with the file in front of them will run. **BOTH ARE RECORDED**, here and in the pin node, so that a reader who computes 801 finds the disagreement explained where they meet it rather than concluding the pin is wrong.
text_pin_ruling.what_a_text_pin_that_has_no_pagination_w: IT WOULD CARRY NO `pages` FIELD, and this is written down before such a document arrives rather than after, because the alternative gets decided in a hurry by whoever meets it. A document with no pagination has no page count; `"pages": 0` would be a COUNT, and a count of zero pages is a false statement about a document somebody can read. `"pages": 1` would be a guess dressed as a measurement. The field is absent, the gates that read it tolerate its absence for a text pin, and `lines` plus `bytes` plus `sha256` carry the identity — which is three terms, and one more than the two a reader needs.
text_pin_ruling.ruling_2_not_committed_uniformly_with_ev: RULED BY M ON 2026-09-04. **THE RFC IS NOT COMMITTED, AND THE GROUND IS ONE MECHANISM FOR EVERY DOCUMENT THIS REPOSITORY PINS RATHER THAN LICENCE.** The distinction is the whole ruling, so it is stated in both directions. WHAT THE LICENCE WOULD PERMIT: RFC 2781's own Full Copyright Statement reads that the document 'may be copied and furnished to others ... without restriction of any kind, provided that the above copyright notice and this paragraph are included on all such copies', so committing it would be permitted outright — unlike STANAG 4609 Edition 5, whose restriction `not_committed.why` quotes and which is the reason that node exists. **AND IT IS STILL NOT COMMITTED.** A repository that vendored the documents it is allowed to vendor and pinned the ones it is not would have TWO mechanisms for holding a document, and a reader could not tell from a pin record which one governed a given row. One mechanism is worth more than the bytes: every pin is a digest plus a route, every held document is in the working tree and out of the index, and `git ls-files` naming nothing under any `fixtures/*/spec/` except `.json` and `.py` is a single invariant rather than a list of exceptions. THE RULE IS THEREFORE A MECHANISM RULE AND MUST NOT BE READ AS A LICENCE CLAIM: `.gitignore`'s `*.txt` says nothing about what RFC 2781 permits, and the comment beside it says so in as many words so that nobody later reads the rule backwards into a restriction the Internet Society did not impose.
text_pin_ruling.the_gitignore_rule_and_why_it_is_global: **A GLOBAL `*.txt`, BESIDE `*.pdf`, AND THE FORK WAS DERIVED RATHER THAN PREFERRED.** The round's own condition: a global rule is safe if the index holds no `.txt` today, and a path-anchored `fixtures/*/spec/*.txt` is required otherwise. `git ls-files '*.txt'` is **0**, so the global rule is safe and is the one taken — on the argument `.gitignore`'s own block makes about `*.pdf`: an EXTENSION rule needs no edit when a thirteenth document arrives in a pinned directory, and a path-anchored rule would have to be widened by every round that adds a `spec/` directory. THE THREE `.txt` POPULATIONS ALREADY IN THE WORKING TREE ARE UNAFFECTED AND WERE CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: `packages/cdm/synapse_cdm.egg-info/*.txt` is already ignored by `.gitignore:8`'s `*.egg-info/`, `fixtures/klv/provenance/*.txt` by `.gitignore:173`'s directory rule — the THIRD rule `not_committed` records — and `docs/node_modules/**/*.txt` by `docs/.gitignore:2`. So the new rule shadows nothing and un-ignores nothing; it adds the one path that would otherwise have staged.
text_pin_ruling.every_gate_widened_and_the_extension_che: **WIDENED TO THE DECLARED FORMAT, NOT LOOSENED.** The instruction this round carried, and the reason it matters: the `.pdf` filters were doing load-bearing work that READ as an extension preference. `tests/test_cdm_pins.py`'s filter is what keeps the two transport-stream artefacts under `fixtures/klv/streams/` and the nine fetched provenance files under `fixtures/klv/provenance/` out of a corpus that resolves every member against the package base — `gates/pin_paths.py`'s docstring records the three reproductions of exactly that. So the filters were not dropped for a format field; `.txt` was ADMITTED BESIDE `.pdf` at each site and the extension check kept, which means a `.klv` stream and a `.txt` provenance capture are refused for two independent reasons now rather than one: the extension, and the fact that no pin record names them. THE PROVENANCE FILES ARE THE SHARP CASE and they are `.txt`: nine of them, under `fixtures/klv/provenance/`, and the widened filters admit `.txt` — so what refuses them is that `spec_pin_files_on_disk()` globs `*/spec` and not `*/provenance`, and that no pin record carries their paths. Both were re-checked by mutation after the widening rather than argued from the code, and the mutation log is at `tests/test_cdm_pins.py::test_a_stream_or_a_provenance_capture_under_a_pin_path_is_still_refused`.
what_this_ruling_does_NOT_do: Does not add `format` to the twelve PDF nodes. Absence means PDF, ruled above, and the alternative was twelve diffs describing bytes that did not move.

Does not touch `gates/parks_table.py`. Its `held_series()` globs `spec.glob("*.pdf")`, so a `.txt` under `spec/` contributes no series number and `FILE_SERIES` gains no `2781` — the surface round predicted this and the reading confirms it. A widening there would have made `2781` read as a MISB four-digit series, which is the exact class of false positive that module's `SERIES` comment refuses.
Does not touch `gates/pin_paths.py`. `discover()` carries no extension filter by design.
Does not make a text pin the preferred form. Where a publisher issues a PDF, the PDF is the copy that is read; this ruling reaches the case where there is none.

Does not change the delegation tally. Fourteen delegations remain in scope. RFC 2781 is the encoding reference of ONE ELEMENT of one held delegation and is not a fifteenth delegation — the same distinction `st_336_2007` draws about itself.
